Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper score back-to-back for Brighton to complete the comeback

The key moments from Old Trafford

8: GOAL! Lacey initially makes it a dream full United debut by skipping past two Brighton defenders before finding the near post

9: GOAL! Forty-three seconds after the restart, Mount makes it 2-0 after Jason Steele saved from Marcus Rashford.

36: BIG CHANCE! Brighton respond well after the early double deficit but Malick Yalcouye curls a one-on-one chance wide.

45+1: GOAL! Kostoulas beats Darlow to a long ball into the box and slots in a leveller, despite United complaints Benjamin Sesko had been fouled in the build-up.

65: GOAL! Gross converts from close range after Sesko headed the ball back to him after losing 50:50.

69: GOAL! Old Trafford is stunned as substitute Diego Gomez goes on lengthy run and crosses for De Cuyper, who finishes from close range.

76: HUGE CHANCE! Rashford is played through on goal but his near-post finish is kept out by Steele.

84: TWO CHANCES! Brighton miss a double chance to seal the game as Kostoulas' effort is cleared off the line by Leny Yoro, before Gomez's shot is saved by Darlow.

Carrick: We can't accept that

Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick to Sky Sports:

"We can't accept that as a group. I take responsibility for it. The performance towards the end of the second half, that's on me.

"We'll all be better. We have to be better. We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We're out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches."

What do you need to do to get better? "We'll get better on a number of things."

Is he feeling the boos from the fans? "Yeah of course, that's pretty obvious! I totally understand the feelings of the supporters.

"We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It's on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I'll take the praise, I'll take the criticism and the upset.

"I totally understand it for the way the game went. We have got to win games."

Analysis: When will it end at Man Utd?

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

Manchester United just haven't changed have they? Year after year of failure.

Go back to August 7 2022; it was a similar picture to now at Old Trafford. That was the day Brighton won 2-1 at Old Trafford with Pascal Gross scoring twice and pulling the strings.

Four years later, at the age of 35, Gross is still pulling those same strings - a sign of the German's great longevity, but also a sign of United's failure to progress anywhere.

That match was 1,502 days ago and saw Erik ten Hag's tenure get off to a horrendous start. United have gone through four other managers in those four years since then. When will it end?

Hurzeler: I didn't think we started that bad!

Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler to Sky Sports:

"We started the game really well. We conceded two easy goals and we stuck to the plan. That was the positive thing.

"When you're 2-0 goal you can go in one direction and say the game is done and don't stick to the plan anymore. Or you have to believe in yourself and the match plan and finish doing it. The longer the game went, the better we were. And we won a deserved win.

"I didn't think we started that bad. We conceded goals and goals change momentum but we had the right structure and good patterns. We weren't clean. The bad thing is we were quite nervous, making technical mistakes and then the players grew into the game.

"In the end, we completely controlled the game. We had plenty of chances to score another goal. But I had a feeling in the beginning that some players were nervous."

Sports.title: Liverpool face Chelsea as Carabao Cup fourth-round draw confirmed
Sports.content:
Liverpool will host Chelsea in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup, while Premier League champions Arsenal have drawn the lowest-ranked side left in the competition, Fleetwood Town.

Xabi Alonso will be set for his first Anfield return as Chelsea boss after his side beat Leeds last week, with the Reds getting past Tottenham on Tuesday.

Alonso, who won the Champions League with Liverpool as a player during a distinguished spell, was touted as a possible replacement for Arne Slot but went to Stamford Bridge instead.

Chelsea's trip to Anfield is one of five all-Premier League clashes, with a potential sixth if Manchester City beat Norwich on Thursday, live on Sky Sports, which would set up a home tie against Brighton, who pulled off a sensational comeback to win at Manchester United.

Sports.title: Everton strike late to beat much-changed Wolves in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Substitute Charly Alcaraz hit a late winner to give Everton a 1-0 home win over much-changed Wolves in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

The victory now tees up a meeting with Newcastle in an all-Premier League tie in the week commencing October 26.

Alcaraz's 80th-minute winner came just three minutes after coming off the bench, and it maintained Everton's unbeaten start to the season.

It was just Alcaraz's second goal for the club, having scored 13 months ago in this competition.

Image: Charly Alcaraz (right)scored Everton's late winner against Wolves in the Carabao Cup

Everton were deserved winners over the Championship side, who made nine changes from last weekend's league win at Sheffield United.

Wolves' goalscoring hero at Bramall Lane, Raul Jimenez, was given a start, but he was concerningly taken off midway through the first half with an injury.

Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto revealed at his post-match press conference that Jimenez will be ruled out of Sunday's Black Country derby against West Brom at Molineux, live on Sky Sports.

Wolves debutant Joao Virginia was in inspired form against his old club as he pulled off a magnificent close-range save to deny Thierno Barry's header in first-half stoppage time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joao Virginia showed incredible reactions to claw away a Thierno Barry header from close range

Virginia's opposite number Jordan Pickford made a good save to deny Jimenez's replacement Adam Armstrong early in the second half, which was the visitors' first shot on target of the game.

Virginia then denied Everton substitute Brennan Johnson, but he could do nothing to stop Alcaraz's powerful curling strike from inside the area late on.

It was a goal that gave on-watching UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his Canadian counterpart and fellow Everton fan Mark Carney plenty of joy as David Moyes' side remain in the hunt to earn their first silverware since 1995.

Image: Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Prime Minister of Canada Mark Carney celebrating Everton's first goal vs Wolves

Dibling's progression hailed after win

Everton assistant manager Alan Irvine believes Tyler Dibling is starting to look like he belongs at the club after a difficult first season.

The 20-year-old was named player of the match in the win after comfortably his best performance of a stuttering first 13 months of his Toffees career as he provided the assist for Alcaraz's winner.

"Since he came back for pre-season, he looks like he belongs here; he looks more comfortable," said Irvine.

"He is a very quiet lad, and it can sometimes take young lads time to settle in, especially at a club like this with the expectation so that was probably difficult for him last year.

"I said to him before the game, 'You've been waiting patiently - or impatiently - and you've now got your chance, and now you must take that opportunity. Make sure the manager has a tough decision to make for the next game,' and he's done that.

"You saw a little moment of that acceleration he has got, and he doesn't show enough of those moments, and he needs to be doing more.

"I've spent a bit of time with Tyler and Tyrique (George) this pre-season trying to get them to contribute more than previously, and there are certainly signs that is coming."

Meanwhile, Peixoto did not regret making nine changes.

He said: "I think we did a good game; we competed against a strong Premier League team.

"I think today a lot of young players did a great job.

"I'm happy with the job today but not with the result."

Sports.title: What is tennis' Laver Cup? Watch Ryder Cup-style event on Sky Sports this month
Sports.content:
Find out all you need to know as 12 of the world's best men's players compete in the annual Europe vs 'Rest of the World' Laver Cup showdown, live on Sky Sports September 25-27.

Earlier this year, Sky Sports agreed a deal with Trident8 to show all three days of the Laver Cup from London's O2 Arena this month.

Here's everything you need to know about tennis' exciting team event...

How does the Laver Cup work?

The event is played over three days, with four matches on the first two days consisting of three singles contests and one doubles. Six players from Team Europe and six from Team World make up the event.

Matches on Friday are worth one point, Saturday two points and Sunday three points. The winner is the first team to reach 13 points.

If the points are level at 12-12 at the end of all matches, there will be a fifth match on Sunday (The Decider).

All matches are best-of-three sets, which progress to a deciding tiebreak if the opening two sets are shared.

In terms of how the individual matches are decided, a blind draw is used to confirm Friday's clashes.

For Saturday's matches, one team picks from a blind draw first, and the other team then selects their players to face those drawn out.

For Sunday, the reverse then takes place as the other team selects from a blind draw, and the opposing team picks which players they want to play thereafter.

Each player must play in at least one singles contest over the first two days, and no player can play in more than two singles matches.

Like golf's Ryder Cup, the venue alternates between Europe and elsewhere per each edition. It has been held annually since 2017.

The 2026 Laver Cup is being staged at London's O2, while the 2027 event will be hosted at the Intuit Dome in Inglewood, Los Angeles.

Image: Alcaraz has played in the Laver Cup in 2024 and 2025, and will do so again in 2026

Which players are competing in the 2026 Laver Cup?

Frenchman Yannick Noah and the USA's Andre Agassi are the respective captains. Britain's Tim Henman is Team Europe's vice-captain, while Australia's Pat Rafter is Team World's vice-captain.

Team Europe lineup: Spain's Carlos Alcaraz, Germany's Alexander Zverev, Italy's Flavio Cobolli, Spain's Rafael Jodar, Czech Republic's Jakub Mensik and Norway's Casper Ruud.

Team World lineup: USA's Ben Shelton, Australia's Alex de Minaur, USA's Taylor Fritz, USA's Learner Tien, Kazakhstan's Alexander Bublik and Argentina's Francisco Cerúndolo.

Who are the defending Laver Cup champions?

In 2025, Team World beat Team Europe 15-9 at the Chase Center in San Francisco.

Image: Team World's Taylor Fritz of the USA lifts the 2025 Laver Cup after defeating Carlos Alcaraz's Team Europe

The first day saw Europe 3-1 ahead after singles wins for Ruud over Reilly Opelka and Mensik over Alex Michelsen, and doubles victory for Alcaraz and Mensik over Fritz and Michelsen.

The second day saw domination from Team World, however, as they won all four contests to take a 9-3 lead - De Minaur beating Zverev, Fritz beating Alcaraz, Cerundolo beating Holger Rune and a doubles pairing of De Minaur and Michelsen beating Ruud and Rune.

On the final day, a doubles pairing of Alcaraz and Ruud beat Michelsen and Opelka, and Alcaraz beat Cerundolo in singles, but it wasn't enough as De Minaur beat Mensik and Fritz beat Zverev to wrap up victory.

Henman: Laver Cup a unique opportunity for watching tennis fans

Team Europe vice-captain and Sky Sports Tennis expert Tim Henman said:

"It's a unique opportunity to see the best players in the world coming together to represent Team Europe and Team World at the iconic O2 arena.

"Fans can expect plenty of drama, passion and rivalry, both on and off the court.

"It's great news the Laver Cup will be on Sky Sports."

Image: Team Europe vice-captain and Sky Sports Tennis expert Tim Henman has called the Laver Cup 'unique'

Watch on Sky Sports Tennis

Hosted by presenter Gigi Salmon, Sky Sports will broadcast all 12 matches across day and night sessions on Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26, followed by a single concluding session on Sunday September 27.

There will also be a reporter on the ground keeping fans abreast of all the news from the weekend's action.

Alongside broadcast rights, fans in the UK and Ireland will also be able to catch up on all the action with clips and highlights available across Sky's digital and social platforms.

Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App. You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: De Cuyper and Brighton pile on pain for Manchester United with comeback
Sports.content:
Across four days Manchester United have lost the 199th derby to Manchester City, were told by JJ Gabriel he wants to leave, and have now been knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton.

Capitulating after being 2-0 up may be the pick of these dizzying blows, and when Marcus Rashford skated in with the chance to take the tie to 3-3 late on, there was no surprise he hit Jason Steele rather than the net.

Towards the end, Matheus Cunha was thrown on to join Bruno Fernandes, also a late substitute, illustrating how desperate Michael Carrick was. Yet Charalampos Kostoulas went close to scoring a second for Brighton, as United could not find a route to cancelling out Maxim De Cuyper’s 69th-minute strike that proved the winner.

After taking only four points from twelve in the league, serious questions will now be asked about where Carrick’s team are heading; they have to beat Fulham on Sunday to start correcting a dismal start to the season.

View image in fullscreen United were frustrated by Pascal Gross’s leveller for Brighton, but things were about to get even worse for Michael Carrick’s side. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Carrick stated Sunday’s injustice against City would give his side an edge and Shea Lacey provided a cutting one when decorating a full debut with the sweetest of goals.

The 19-year-old shimmied in Brighton’s area, beating Jaouen Hadjam before firing beyond a helpless Jason Steele. As impressive here was Benjamin Sesko’s hold-up work in the buildup as this allowed red shirts to flood forward, Youri Tielemans feeding Lacey.

This was seven minutes in and less than 120 seconds later Mason Mount doubled United’s advantage.

Rashford’s pace and drive took him clear along the left, again inside the area. A trailing Steele boot saved the No 9’s effort but the ball bounced into Mount’s path and he drove home, via the turf, for a first goal since a win at Wolves last December.

Lacey’s strike drew a Carrick grin and delight from Mount, and you wondered how Gabriel – earmarked for this game’s squad, with the chance to become United’s youngest ever player – felt.

View image in fullscreen United’s evening started brightly enough, with the 19-year-old Shea Lacey scoring on his first start for the club. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Brighton had lost only one of their last five visits here, with a flying start to the league campaign placing Fabian Hürzeler’s team in fifth. Yet Sunday’s 5-0 hammering of Coventry already seemed distant as United continued to dominate.

Olivier Boscagli hit a corner straight out, summing up the visitors’ start, before Matt O’Riley forced Ayden Heaven into an error that led to another. This presaged a Seagulls renaissance that featured a lightning Malick Yalcouyé break but, clear in on the debutant Karl Darlow’s goal, the Ivorian spooned wide. The No 35 lacked the sharpness evident in a Rashford nutmeg of Chema Andrés which embarrassed the Brighton man and when Pascal Gross blasted over this was one more chance spurned by Hürzeler’s men.

But then came a goal – and real hope – for Brighton. Hadjam’s long left-right diagonal cut United’s rearguard clean out, and the slumbering Heaven allowed Kostoulas to scamper free, the striker beating Darlow through his legs.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Carrick, having beaten only Ipswich so far this season, needed a win, and as United (not under him) exited at the earliest time of both cup competitions last year, progressing to at least a second tie in one of them would be welcome.

View image in fullscreen Charalampos Kostoulas started Brighton’s comeback just before half-time. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

A wild Tielemans long-range shot that ballooned over failed to restore United’s two-goal lead but at least the home unit were tapping the ball about, operating in Brighton territory, moving the guests around.

A Sesko burst from halfway had the onrushing Steele hacking away just in time so United were in control. But the question was: could they maintain this and register the type of mature, accomplished display that would show an evolution in Carrick’s team? Sesko, in yards of space, dawdling and dispossessed when a simple ball would have fed Lacey, suggested not.

A loose Rashford pass aimed for Sesko – the same. More promising was a pass for Noussair Mazraoui as he drove into the area along the left channel. As was the subsequent corner that created an opening for Tielemans to narrowly miss.

Quick Guide Carabao Cup roundup: Fleetwood handed win over Blades Show A 57th-minute Rhys Norrington-Davies own goal sent Fleetwood into the last 16 of the Carabao Cup for the first time as the League Two club stunned their Championship opponents, Sheffield United, 1-0 at Highbury, before pulling a home tie against Arsenal out in the draw. Matt Lawlor’s side, unbeaten now in nine games in all competitions, had another Danny Andrew effort ruled out for offside and twice hit the woodwork in a dominant second-half display. It was a searching left-wing cross from Andrew that Norrington-Davies nodded beyond Michael Cooper to give the fourth-tier club a historic victory. Tom Cannon did get the ball in the net for Chris Wilder’s visitors who lined up with only four starting survivors from last Friday’s 1-0 league defeat by Wolves. But a flag for offside was raised before the striker slid the ball into the net. United started positively and Ollie Arblaster had a goalbound effort blocked after only 36 seconds. But Mark Helm forced Cooper into a seventh-minute save before the former United forward Ched Evans put his follow-up header narrowly wide. Jay Lynch denied Joe Rothwell as the visitors attacked again but Cooper was the busier, saving from Lewis McCann and Crispin McLean. Helm’s dipping right-foot effort from 18 yards grazed the top netting as Fleetwood finished the first half in the ascendancy and they deserved their break from Norrington-Davies’ own goal. United finally came to life in the last 10 minutes with Lynch brilliantly denied Sydie Peck and Ben Brereton Díaz, while Cannon saw a goalbound strike superbly blocked. Everton’s forgotten man Charly Alcaraz stepped up when his side needed some inspiration to score the only goal in the win over Wolves three minutes after coming on. The Argentinian had played just 14 minutes all season but belied his lack of match sharpness with a quick switch of the ball from one foot to the other to guide a left-footed shot past the former Everton goalkeeper João Virgínia in the 80th minute. It also represented a minor success for Tyler Dibling, whose career has not really taken off since his £35m move from Southampton just over a year ago, as he claimed the assist at the end his most encouraging performance for the club. Everton's reward is a home tie against Newcastle. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

But then disaster. Diogo Dalot’s hoofed clearance failed to find Sesko as Luka Vuskovic headed to Gross; Brighton’s captain made room and netted with ease. Even worse followed. Brighton raided along the right, Kostoulas’s cross pinged off Mazraoui’s backside, and there was De Cuyper to finish.

On 72 minutes Carrick played his ace, introducing Fernandes for Mount, then followed up with Cunha. But United remained toothless.

Sports.title: Tammy Abraham’s double powers Aston Villa to Carabao Cup win at Coventry
Sports.content:
For Aston Villa, an overdue drama-free outing as Unai Emery’s side cruised into the Carabao Cup fourth round courtesy of a Tammy Abraham double and a Ross Barkley header.

Unfortunately for Coventry, it was a sorry case of more of the same. Frank Lampard’s side have lost five of their six matches in all competitions and continue to leak soft goals. It was hard to know whether Abraham’s tap-in or Barkley’s free header, both from corners, was worse from a Coventry perspective. The sight of Lampard hunched in the dugout, hands clasped, has become a familiar sight.

These teams came into this game in search of a much-needed lift, both Coventry and Villa winless in the Premier League. Lampard’s side, who have lost their opening four matches by an aggregate of 10-0 and on Saturday visit Nottingham Forest hoping for lift-off, have only scored this season in this competition. Victor Torp’s sweet free-kick from the edge of Villa’s 18-yard box, to cancel out Abraham’s first goal of the season, represented Coventry’s first goal since Torp capped the scoring at Plymouth in the previous round.

This was the first competitive meeting between these sides since 5 May 2001, when Coventry’s 34-year stay in the top flight came to an end after defeat at Villa Park. They may be peers now they are back together in the same division but, despite Coventry’s £130m summer spend, in some ways they remain in different leagues. Villa handed Ibrahim Mbaye, a £47m buy from Paris Saint-Germain, and Matteo Ruggeri, a £17m purchase from Atlético Madrid, their first starts, while there was a full debut for Taylor Harwood-Bellis, the £25m arrival from Southampton. Attempting to close the gap has so far proved a thankless task.

But a flag for offside was raised before the striker slid the ball into the net. United started positively and Ollie Arblaster had a goalbound effort blocked after only 36 seconds. But Mark Helm forced Cooper into a seventh-minute save before the former United forward Ched Evans put his follow-up header narrowly wide. Jay Lynch denied Joe Rothwell as the visitors attacked again but Cooper was the busier, saving from Lewis McCann and Crispin McLean. Helm’s dipping right-foot effort from 18 yards grazed the top netting as Fleetwood finished the first half in the ascendancy and they deserved their break from Norrington-Davies’ own goal. United finally came to life in the last 10 minutes with Lynch brilliantly denied Sydie Peck and Ben Brereton Díaz, while Cannon saw a goalbound strike superbly blocked. Everton’s forgotten man Charly Alcaraz stepped up when his side needed some inspiration to score the only goal in the win over Wolves three minutes after coming on. The Argentinian had played just 14 minutes all season but belied his lack of match sharpness with a quick switch of the ball from one foot to the other to guide a left-footed shot past the former Everton goalkeeper João Virgínia in the 80th minute. It also represented a minor success for Tyler Dibling, whose career has not really taken off since his £35m move from Southampton just over a year ago, as he claimed the assist at the end his most encouraging performance for the club. Everton's reward is a home tie against Newcastle. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Lampard made nine changes from Sunday’s bruising 5-0 defeat by Brighton but when Aurèle Amenda limped off through injury on 10 minutes, Bobby Thomas, wearing the captain’s armband, was the only player left from their previous starting XI. Emery made seven changes himself and George Hemmings, one of those to keep their place, was the architect for Villa’s opener, Abraham coolly rolling the ball past Dan Bentley. Ruggeri fed Hemmings down the left and the 19-year-old sent a sumptuous pass into Abraham with the outside of his right boot.

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard shows his disappointment as Coventry suffer another defeat. Photograph: Getty Images/Sportsphoto/Allstar

Coventry struggled to retain possession and Villa were enjoying themselves, exchanging crisp, clean passes. But then Barkley was penalised for fouling Caleb Yirenkyi on the edge of the Villa box and Torp stepped up to lift the subsequent free-kick over the Villa wall. John McGinn, the Villa captain reduced to the role of draught excluder, picked himself up from the turf. Suddenly Coventry were full of confidence, a little giddy even. Thomas moonlighted as a striker, forcing an error from Tyrone Mings but then declined a golden opportunity to shoot at goal and the chance fizzled out. Gustavo Hamer then sent a left-foot shot just past the Villa upright.

Coventry were reborn but Villa responded. McGinn spurned a decent chance for Villa, drilling a first-time shot into the side-netting. McGinn smacked his hands together in frustration. A few minutes later Barkley sent a low drive at goal that Bentley did well to push wide for a corner, from which Villa prospered. Mbaye’s inswinging delivery was on the money and Barkley, totally unmarked in the six-yard box, headed in at the front post to regain Villa’s lead.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Coventry had the meanest defence in the Championship last season but have been porous since promotion. More slack marking enabled Villa to extend their lead from another corner. McGinn, presumably heartened by an ovation from the sold-out away end behind him, whipped the ball into the six-yard box and Abraham prodded in after walking off his marker, the 18-year-old Coventry debutant Stephen Mfuni, who this month joined on loan from Manchester City.

Abraham’s second gave Villa welcome breathing space. Emery, whose side visit Tottenham on Saturday, felt comfortable enough to withdraw McGinn and Mbaye, Emi Buendía and £52m club-record signing Johan Manzambi arriving in their places. Zion Suzuki replaced the injured Marco Bizot in goal at half-time. Nicolas Jackson replaced Abraham with 69 minutes on the clock.

Villa could afford to relax if not fully recline, victory safely stowed. Up in the directors’ box, the Coventry owner, Doug King, legs crossed, looked on pensively. Lampard stewed in the home dugout. Four months on from promotion, it is amazing how quickly the mood music can change.

Sports.title: ‘My scar, not your scar’: Tuchel stands by England semi-final subs but admits wrong timing
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel stands by his heavily criticised defensive substitutions in the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina this summer, but the England head coach accepts he made them too early.

Tuchel said England were “waiting for death”, unable to cope with the attacking tactics adopted by Argentina in Atlanta as they chased the game after Anthony Gordon’s opener on the hour. He said fatigue and the success of defending with a back five in knockout games against Mexico and Norway also influenced his decisions to sit on the lead.

That approach proved catastrophic as goals from Enzo Fernández and Lautaro Martínez in the final stages of the game ended England’s dreams of making a first World Cup final since 1966.

“You can try to kill me here. But it’s my scar, it’s not your scar,” Tuchel said in a documentary on the England app. “No one is more hurt than me, no one wanted it more. They can endlessly torture you and think: ‘If I had done different substitutions, then we would have won the match.’ You just don’t know it.

“Of course you could [have made attacking changes]. No one knows what would have happened. We could have done it and maybe lost 2‑1 and could have gone: ‘Is he crazy? He finished the game against Norway with a back five, why didn’t he finish the game with five?’ I think from what I saw and the experience, the information and the level of craziness Argentina put in – change after change after change, it was just one offensive change after the other. That was my solution to the problem.

“That’s what the intervention of a coach is. I try to help, you don’t implement anything for your ego or whatever. You just try to help.”

View image in fullscreen Jordan Pickford is beaten by Enzo Fernández’s shot for Argentina’s first goal. Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/Reuters

England were on the back foot after scoring, with Djed Spence making a last-ditch tackle and Jordan Pickford making a big save immediately before the hydration break. It was then when Tuchel made his ill-fated decision to replace the goalscorer Gordon with the defender Ezri Konsa.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The German, who faced calls to be sacked in the aftermath of the semi-final defeat, insists the opposition’s gung-ho tactics forced his hand. “Argentina then play very, very quickly. Sorry for the language, [they played] fuck-it football: ‘We have nothing to lose. Let’s fuck it.’ A key moment if I look back at it and what happened to my decision-making, we conceded a big, big chance right before the water break. And I thought: ‘We will not survive. This is waiting for death. We don’t have ball possession, we’re not defending good, we’re not defending properly in our 4-4-2. We need help.’

“I changed to a 5-3-2, we changed the structure. Because I believe we can handle the width better and we still have three central defenders in the middle if crosses still fly in. We changed then to a 5-4-1. Even my mindset is maybe like: ‘Let’s just overcome it.’ And it’s too early. Too early for that mindset.”

Sports.title: Saudi Pro League club Al-Taawoun handed stadium ban over Diogo Jota chants
Sports.content:
The Saudi Pro League club Al-Taawoun have been fined nearly £20,000 and given a two-game stadium ban after fans chanted about the late Liverpool and Portugal forward Diogo Jota.

The Al-Hilal midfielder Rúben Neves, who played with Jota for Wolves and Portugal, was shown gesturing to the sky after audible chants of “Jota” from Al-Taawoun fans could be heard during Saturday’s league game.

Jota died in July 2025 along with his brother, André ‌Silva, in a car crash in Spain and Neves was one of the pallbearers at his funeral.

A statement from the Saudi Football Federation read: “The fans of Al-Taawoun chanted phrases and slogans that violated the provisions of the disciplinary and ethics regulations, and the committee decided to increase the penalty in accordance with (39-4) of the disciplinary and ethics regulations.”

The federation ordered Al-Taawoun to play their next two home league matches behind closed doors and fined the club 100,000 riyals (£19,800).

Cristiano Ronaldo, who plays for the rival club Al-Nassr, had called for the fans that chanted about his former international teammate to be punished with stadium lifetime bans.

Sports.title: Enzo Le Fée makes amends from the spot as Sunderland overcome AZ
Sports.content:
Sunderland’s captain, Granit Xhaka, believes it is not unrealistic to dream about Régis Le Bris’s side travelling all the way to next spring’s Europa League final.

It is rarely a good idea to dismiss Xhaka but reaching that showpiece in Frankfurt will necessitate considerably more efficient finishing on his team’s part than proved evident on a highly evocative night on Wearside.

Thanks to a second-half penalty from the indefatigable Enzo Le Fée –appropriately the game’s outstanding player – it ended happily as Sunderland launched their big return to Europe with a morale-boosting win. Along the way, though, they missed far too many chances for Le Bris’ liking.

Sunderland’s European comeback was sandwiched between last Saturday’s home Premier League defeat to Arsenal and this weekend’s trip to Manchester City. The latter assignment surely informed Le Bris’ decision to indulge in a little light rotation and leave Brian Brobbey, Dan Ballard and Thomas Meunier resting their legs on the home bench at kick-off.

Occupants of the VIP seats included Jimmy Montgomery, the now 82-year-old hero of Sunderland’s 1973 FA Cup triumph against Leeds and their goalkeeper during that last, albeit fairly short lived, European adventure in the Cup Winners’ Cup 53 years ago.

View image in fullscreen Sunderland put on an impressive fireworks display before their first European game in 53 years. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

Down on the pitch, Malick Fofana, the winger signed from Lyon for £30m on transfer deadline day, made his first start following a spine-tingling, ear-splitting, preamble to kick-off featuring a giant tifo of a sailing ship floating above the message: “New shores to conquer”.

Not that AZ were inclined to surrender lightly. Leeroy Echteld’s team arrived having enjoyed an unbeaten start to the season, winning five and drawing one of their opening Eredivisie games. Indeed they would have assumed a very early lead on Wearside had Sunderland’s Dutch goalkeeper Robin Roefs not extended a boot and kept out Ro-Zangelo Daal’s low shot. The moment had arrived for Le Fée to raise the home tone and his half-volley duly tested Jari De Busser before Wilson Isidor failed to make contact with Le Fée’s inviting delivery from the rebound.

Though De Busser was swiftly forced to push Kevin Danso’s fine shot over the bar, Sunderland nearly came undone on the counter-attack and it took on excellent interception on Trai Hume’s part to halt Ayoub Oufkir in his tracks.

Oufkir and the talented visiting No 10, Kees Smit, issued timely reminders that AZ are more than merely deft in possession but Le Bris’ starting XI was hardly shabby either and, after Isidor conjured a glorious chance, Le Fée’s shot hit the post.

Quick Guide Benfica dispatch Amorim's Milan Show Ruben Amorim’s Milan were beaten 2-0 by Marco Silva’s Benfica in the Europa League. Dodi Lukebakio put the Portuguese side ahead at San Siro in the 16th minute and Jakub Kaminski added a second early in the second half. Bayer Leverkusen, finalists in 2024, began their Europa League campaign with a 2-0 win against the Slovenian champions Celje while Lyon were 2-1 winners at Anderlecht. The Cypriot champions Omonia Nicosia stunned the La Liga side Celta Vigo 1-0 while Rangers’ conquerors Jagiellonia Bialystok were denied a point at the Greek giants Olympiacos by Roman Yaremchuk’s late winner. Sparta Prague thrashed Ararat-Armenia 4-1 while Sturm Graz against Rennes and Hapoel Be’er Sheva versus Dinamo Zagreb both ended goalless. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

It was not long before another shot, from Hume this time, whizzed fractionally wide of an upright. It is worth remembering that when Hume joined Sunderland, back in January 2022, they were in League One.

Back in the present Le Bris’ team ended the first half thoroughly dominant but unable to convert a litany of chances. Oufkir, meanwhile, was a little fortunate to have collected only a yellow card after sliding in recklessly on Le Fée. Echteld withdrew Oufkir at the interval, replacing him with Weslley Patati.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

AZ re-emerged for the new half apparently invigorated and it was easy to see why Smit has collected admirers at some of Europe’s biggest clubs. After watching him turning Sunderland’s defence inside out before curling a shot inches wide with Roefs stranded, Le Bris took the precaution of replacing the already booked Omar Alderete with Ballard.

View image in fullscreen Le Fée fires home the decisive penalty. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

The hosts almost took the lead when Le Fée’s stellar pass picked out Isidor but the centre-forward could not quite polish it off. When Hume subsequently missed a presentable chance it felt like De Busser’s goal must be protected by some sort of magnetic forcefield.

Then Patati fouled Le Fée in the area as he shaped to shoot and the Frenchman stepped up to the spot. Having seen his penalty against Arsenal saved expertly by David Raya, Le Fée looked a little nervous but sent De Busser the wrong way as he struck a textbook kick low into the bottom corner.

With Brobbey by now liberated from the bench, Sunderland briefly pushed for a second goal and Nordi Mukiele went close with a header following Xhaka’s corner.

Not that AZ were quite out of it. With Smit withdrawn, the talented Daal came to the fore and his tight close control and ability to run with the ball perhaps prompted a change of home tactic as Le Bris’ players sat back and defended their lead. It made the final 10 minutes extremely nervy inside the Stadium of Light but Le Fée and co had done just enough to launch their European galleon.

Sports.title: ‘They are very similar’: Arsenal’s Dowman reminds Merino of Lamine Yamal
Sports.content:
Mikel Merino says Max Dowman reminds him of Lamine Yamal after the Arsenal prodigy continued his development by scoring twice in his side’s 4-2 win against Ipswich.

Dowman, who has been given a host of opportunities at senior level by Mikel Arteta, starred after being handed his first appearance of the season, at Portman Road on Tuesday. The 16-year-old attacker’s classy double eased Arsenal into the last 16 of the Carabao Cup and left Arteta admitting that containing the hype around the England youth international is not an easy task.

Arsenal are managing Dowman carefully and Merino is well placed to see how young talents can benefit from listening to managers and older players. The Arsenal midfielder plays with Lamine Yamal for Spain and believes Dowman is as fearless as the 19-year-old winger.

“There are some similarities in terms of their character,” he said. “They don’t care about the spotlight. They thrive when pressure is at the highest. They are always up for the challenge and they are not shy at all – even facing the biggest names in the game.”

Merino, who also scored against Ipswich, raved about Dowman. “He is an unbelievable talent. We knew it, but every time he goes on the pitch and plays against grown men he makes the difference. He is a big talent and we have to take care of him.

“We have to keep pushing him. He needs to keep learning – eyes and ears open always. There is still big room for improvement in a lot of areas and he knows that. So we are going to be by his side trying to get him to his best level.

“It is a thin line. It is very difficult to have equilibrium sometimes with him, because obviously you want him to shine and show everyone the talent that he has. But you have to sometimes remind them that they are human beings and they are part of a bigger squad and team.

“The good thing with these kind of players – Lamine and Max – is that they are special talents, but at the same time they are very humble. They are always keen to learn and listen to the veterans. That is priceless.”

Merino also praised Marli Salmon after the 17-year-old impressed against Ipswich. “In that position as a centre-back, you need to be very mature,” he said.

“It’s very important you don’t make many mistakes. Every action is crucial. It’s the same as with Max, he is an unbelievable talent. We try to teach them our experience and they are very good at listening.”

Sports.title: Lewis Koumas on playing ‘the Liverpool way’, showing hunger and hopes for the future
Sports.content:
With a man of the match award in one hand and his phone in the other, Lewis Koumas made a very important call before stopping to speak to the media at Anfield on Tuesday night. What it means to represent your boyhood club, and to shine for it, was apparent for all to see.

“That was my mum,” said the Liverpool forward, still beaming from the award Cody Gakpo handed to him after the 3-1 Carabao Cup third-round win over Tottenham. “She was here tonight with my nan, my grandad and my sister. They were all in the box. I rang them straight away to show them the trophy and they were buzzing.”

What it takes to impress Andoni Iraola and function effectively in his front line was also apparent from Koumas’s performance against Spurs. The Liverpool head coach had aimed a pre-match dig at more decorated, expensive names when calling for better pressing and tenacity from his forwards in light of Saturday’s flat draw with Fulham. Koumas was not part of that conversation but, as he worked himself to a standstill against the Spurs defence, creating space and opportunities for others to exploit, it seemed the 20-year-old had taken Iraola’s comments to heart as well as on board.

“The energy he shows is contagious,” Iraola said. “I’m very happy for him. He does it in training every day. He is very clear what he needs to do, what the team needs.”

Koumas, who celebrates his 21st birthday on Saturday, the day before Liverpool travel to Bournemouth, Iraola’s former club, took the compliment in his humble, studious stride. “How I play is ultimately the Liverpool way,” he said. “We’ve always been a club where players have to give absolutely everything on the pitch. We’re bringing that back now and the crowd are loving it.

View image in fullscreen Lewis Koumas came close to scoring in the first half against Spurs at Anfield. Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty Images

“A lot of it is about what I do off the ball. The gaffer has shown trust to me that I can carry out his plans in terms of how we want to play tactically. I was happy to do that for him. It gives me so much motivation the fact he’s putting me in for a game like this. I want to kick on now.”

Iraola placed trust in the Chester‑born forward within weeks of his arrival this summer, informing Liverpool’s then sporting director, Richard Hughes, that he wanted Koumas in the first‑team squad and not sent out on loan again. Having impressed on the pre-season tour of the US, Koumas, the son of the former Tranmere and West Brom playmaker Jason, has made his first appearances in the Premier League and Champions League as a substitute and now has a first man of the match award at senior level.

Could he have imagined that at the start of pre-season? “No, I would have woken up,” the Wales international says. “I would have thought I was dreaming. I’m just really happy and very grateful for the opportunities I’ve been given. You never know when your last time on the pitch for Liverpool is going to be. I just try to leave everything out there every time.”

Koumas has been capped 12 times for Wales, but has had to bide his time to break through at club level. The forward, who can also operate on the wing, was given his first Liverpool start by Jürgen Klopp more than two years ago and marked his full debut with a goal in a 3-0 FA Cup fifth round win over Southampton. He did not feature for his boyhood team again until Iraola arrived, spending the 2024-25 campaign on loan at Stoke, the first half of 2025-26 on loan to Birmingham and the remainder of that season on loan to Hull.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Lewis Koumas scores Liverpool's first goal in their 3-0 win against Southampton in the FA Cup fifth round in February 2024. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

“I never showed a weak mentality about how the future would look for me at Liverpool,” said Koumas, who cites Michael Owen and Gareth Bale as childhood inspirations. “I always had the drive that I would get here.

“The reason for going out on loan was to prepare for this moment. A lot of hunger can be lost in the game with how things go. But coming through the pre-academy and right through the academy, my hunger has always been there. My hunger comes from representing Liverpool Football Club, wanting to give everything for the best club in the world.”

Sports.title: Maresca says Manchester City still waiting for apology after disputed 2023 derby goal
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has said Manchester United cannot complain about the controversial derby winner on Sunday because Manchester City are still awaiting an apology from the referees’ chief, Howard Webb, for a match-defining decision in the same fixture three years ago.

City lost at Old Trafford in 2023 after Bruno Fernandes equalised despite an offside Marcus Rashford running close to the through ball from which his teammate scored. Maresca was Pep Guardiola’s assistant at the time and had to witness Rashford’s winner a few minutes later.

“The goal was not a regular goal, if you remember,” Maresca said. “And to be honest, no one apologised. We are still waiting for the apology for that goal. Sometimes it happens for you, sometimes it happens against you. It’s football.”

City host Norwich on Thursday in the Carabao Cup, a competition which provides Maresca with the first opportunity to win a trophy at the club. Guardiola won it on a record five occasions.

Phil Foden will not be involved after being sent off against United for kicking out at Fernandes, receiving a three-match ban. “At half-time, he was very sad, very upset because he knew there was something wrong,” Maresca said. “Then after the game he was a little bit more relieved, he was a little bit more happy. And then yesterday he was very good. He knows the reaction was not a good one, but again, it’s finished and we move on.”

Maresca, who worked as head coach of City’s under-21s and had five graduates reach the first team, could offer opportunities to youngsters as well as fringe players. The teenagers Ryan McAidoo, Kaden Braithwaite and Floyd Samba, son of the former Blackburn defender Chris, will be in the squad, having spent the season with the first-team group.

“When we started pre-season we had many young players and then at the end we decided to keep just these three players,” Maresca said. “They can work with us every day, they can improve, and at some point they can also get a chance to get some minutes.”

The Brazilian attacker Allan and the Argentinian goalkeeper Gerónimo Rulli could make debuts after joining in the summer. Jérémy Doku is making good progress in his rehabilitation from a calf injury picked up in the Community Shield.

Sports.title: Relegation-threatened EFL clubs confirm match has been postponed
Sports.content:
MK Dons have announced their League One fixture against Bromley has been postponed due to international call-ups.

The Dons were initially due to host the Ravens at Stadium MK on Saturday September 26 in a 3pm kick-off.



3 MK Dons' home clash with Bromley at Stadium MK will be played at a later date

It promised to be an early relegation six-pointer, with the two sides struggling at the foot of the table after six games.

MK Dons sit 20th in League One on five points, having failed to win a game, while Bromley are currently 22nd on the same points tally.

MK Dons announce postponement

It has now been announced that League One clash has been postponed due to several of Bromley’s first team players having international call-ups.



While the individuals in question weren't named, this clearly met the EFL's criteria required to reschedule a game.

Per EFL rules, clubs can request a fixture postponement if a player called up for international duty is named in the starting line-up or was a substitute and entered the match before the 75th minute in either 50 per cent of their club's first team matches to date or four of the club's previous five first team games.



With a rescheduled date for the fixture yet to be confirmed, MK Dons reassured fans they would be informed of new details in due course.

Announcing the news in a statement, the club wrote: "MK Dons can confirm that the home match against Bromley set for Saturday 26th September has been postponed.



"The Dons were set to play Bromley on Saturday 26th September at Stadium MK for a 3pm kick-off.

"The match has now been postponed due to several of Bromley’s First Team players having international call-ups.

"Supporters who have already purchased a ticket for this fixture, please note that your ticket will still be valid to use for the rearranged fixture date."

3 Bromley midfielder Ashley Charles has been capped eight times by Grenada Credit: Getty



Bromley's international players

Most national teams are set to announce their squads for the upcoming three-week international break in the coming days.

Five members of Bromley's first-team group have previously been capped internationally.

Midfielder Ashley Charles represents Grenada, while centre-back Deon Woodman is a Kenya international.

On top of this, Will Hondermark, Jacob Mendy and Kamil Conteh play for the Republic of Congo, Gambia and Sierre Leone respectively.



How have both teams performed this season?

As mentioned, both sides have endured difficult starts to their respective League One campaigns.

MK Dons remain the only team in the division who have failed to win a single game, drawing five times and losing once.

3 Former Rotherham and Derby boss Paul Warne has overseen a difficult start to the season at MK Dons Credit: Getty

This leaves Paul Warne's side just above the relegation places on goal difference, with their only defeat coming against Wigan where they were beaten 3-1.



Meanwhile Bromley have struggled so far in their first-ever season in League One after winning promotion last term.

The south London have suffered three defeats in their opening six games, as well as drawing twice and winning just once.

Bromley's only win came away to Barnsley in August, with Victor Adeboyejo scoring the only goal of the game to give them their first win at this level.

Sports.title: Premier League boss urges Thomas Tuchel to pick uncapped 26-year-old for England
Sports.content:
Daniel Farke has insisted Jayden Bogle should be considered for an England call-up alongside Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

The two players starred in Leeds' 4-1 thrashing of Newcastle on Monday, with both playing starring roles.

5 Leeds are in great form at the start of the season as they lie third in the Premier League table Credit: AFP

Victory saw the Whites continue their excellent start to the season, who sit third in the Premier League with eight points from four games.

Striker Calvert-Lewin boosted his case for an England recall by grabbing his third goal of the campaign against the Magpies.

He has since had his goal tally boosted to four, after Bogle was initially awarded the opening goal on Monday night.

Calvert-Lewin assumed he had doubled Leeds' lead at Elland Road when he rose to meet James Justin's header, but he headed the ball off Bogle before it ended up in the back of the net.

However, they submitted an appeal to ensure he got the goal, with the Premier League since awarding the frontman.

Farke highlights Bogle form

There has been plenty of debate over whether Calvert-Lewin's form merits a recall for England's September upcoming Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic and Croatia.

However, Leeds boss Farke was quick to highlight the impressive performances of right-back Bogle of late.

The 26-year-old, a £5million signing from Sheffield United in 2024, has played a key part in Leeds’ impressive run of just five defeats in their past 29 league games.

Initially discussing Calvert-Lewin's England hopes, Farke said: “Definitely realistic, but there are a few other names on my mind with an English passport after a performance like this.”

Asked whether by this he meant a potential Bogle call-up, he added: “Yes, and he also has an English passport. Yes, I agree.”

5 Bogle has made 89 appearances in all competitions since joining Leeds in 2024 Credit: AFP

5 Calvert-Lewin's continued goalscoring form for Leeds has forced him into the England conversation this year Credit: Getty

While Bogle had his goal against Newcastle taken away by Calvert-Lewin, he still earned plenty of plaudits for his performance.

He was named Leeds' Player of the Match in the thumping win as he impressed with his tireless running down the right flank.

The Derby academy graduate's electric form was recently rewarded with a new four-year contract at Elland Road.

Having been capped four times by England at Under-20 level, Bogle will now be eagerly awaiting Thomas Tuchel's upcoming announcement.

The Three Lions boss will name his latest squad on Friday morning, ahead of a new-look three-week international break.

Calvert-Lewin debate rumbles on

While Farke put forward a case for Bogle to earn his first senior England call-up, much of the debate has centred around Calvert-Lewin's hopes of an international renaissance.

5 Just one of Calvert-Lewin's 12 England caps have come under Thomas Tuchel's tutelage Credit: AFP

Having earned a recall earlier this year after a five-year absence, the striker has scored four goals in 12 appearances for his country.

And while his strong club form has seen him tipped to return to the fold, ex-Aston Villa forward Gabby Agbolahor has argued against this, insisting Saud-based duo Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney remain better options.

He told talkSPORT Breakfast: "I just don't think he's [Calvert-Lewin] at the level of what I want for my England striker, I just don't think he is."

Agbonlahor was then asked whether he still believes that Toney and Watkins are ahead of Calvert-Lewin in the selection process.

To which he said: "I think they're better players than Calvert-Lewin, I think they offer something different.

“His hold-up play was good last night, listen, the header actually would have been his goal. Took his second goal, and I think he scored, very well. But I just think there's something missing with Calvert-Lewin.”

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel could leave Man United in £300k deal but must abide by little-known rules to seal Real Madrid transfer
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel could leave Man United in £300k deal but must abide by little-known rules to seal Real Madrid transfer

JJ Gabriel's dream move to Real Madrid could encounter a stumbling block due to FIFA rules on international transfers for under 18s.

The Manchester United wonderkid sent shockwaves on Tuesday when it was revealed that he had asked to leave Old Trafford.



3 Wonderkid Gabriel has dropped a bombshell and asked to leave Man United Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands Real Madrid are now leading the race for Gabriel's signature but face competition from Barcelona and two Premier League clubs.

While the 15-year-old is being hotly pursued, his preferred destination is understood to be the Bernabeu.

Real Madrid complications

A departure from Old Trafford may well prove complicated for Gabriel, with several potential stumbling blocks emerging.



talkSPORT understands JJ Gabriel's family plan to relocate to Spain.

However, FIFA rules stipulate that if a player under age of 18 moves countries he must provide proof his family are moving to that country for 'non-footballing reasons'.

This could throw some doubt over his dream move to Madrid, even though his Irish passport could help his case.



Brexit rules mean English players must be 18 to join a team in Europe, unless they are a dual national with a EU country, subject to FIFA approval.

With Gabriel turning 16 on October 6, he had asked to leave the club ahead of his birthday next month, and his EU citizenship could be crucial in facilitating this.



However, there is no guarantee that FIFA will allow the move to happen, with previous cases being rejected.

In 2005, 16-year-old Paraguayan Carlos Javier Caballero's move to Cadiz in Spain was rejected.

3 Gabriel is viewed as a generational talent, and netted 23 times in 23 U18 Premier League fixtures last term Credit: Getty

The teenager's mum got a job at a restaurant in Spain but FIFA ruled the exception to article 19 - which prohibits the international transfers of Under 18s - was not valid as her finding employment was directly linked to his move.



FIFA rules aren't the only obstacle Gabriel faces, with Man United also able to reject his formal notice to cancel his registration with the club.

Should the Red Devils block his request, his next port of call would be to appeal to the Premier League.

Premier League rules state: “During your child’s registration period, their registration may only be cancelled if everyone agrees (the club, player and their parent/carer).

“If the parties don’t agree, then any person involved can also ask the Premier League to provide a binding decision on a termination request."



Meanwhile if Gabriel moves to an overseas club, United are expected to only receive around £300,000 in training compensation.

3 Gabriel spent pre-season with United's first team and was set to be in the squad for their Carabao Cup clash with Brighton Credit: Getty

Man United told to fight for Gabriel

In the wake of the bombshell news, the Red Devils have been urged to do all they can to keep hold of the youngster - who has been dubbed the 'kid Lionel Messi'.

talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook said on Tuesday's Breakfast Show: "I think optically it's a really bad look if Manchester United lose somebody who Ryan Giggs has gone on record as saying he's a generational talent



"Particularly if he was to join another English club, it probably tells you where United are at in terms of pulling power."

Gabriel was due to be named in United's matchday squad for their Carabao Cup third round clash against Brighton on Wednesday evening, live on talkSPORT.

But the latest developments have inevitably led to Gabriel not being involved.

He would have become United's youngest ever player, with former goalkeeper David Gaskell the incumbent record holder after he played his first game aged 16 years and 19 days.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan predicts Man City’s 115 charges saga could drag on ‘until end of the decade’
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan predicts Man City’s 115 charges saga could drag on ‘until end of the decade’

Simon Jordan thinks that Manchester City's 115 alleged financial breaches has potential to drag on for another FOUR years.

City have been accused of breaking 115 financial regulations, by the Premier League, with another 15 charges later added. The club has always denied any wrongdoing.

2 Man City's case was heard over two years ago, but we still appear no closer to finding a verdict Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The actual hearing lasted 12 weeks and started two years ago today, but there is still no outcome.

And Jordan predicts a scenario where it drags on until the end of this decade.

Speaking on White and Jordan with Jim White and Danny Murphy, the former Crystal Palace owner shared his view on the ongoing wait for a verdict.

He said: "I said it would take a long time, it has taken a long time. It is their own fault.

"They shouldn't have gone for 115 charges. They should have picked five or six meaningful ones and delivered some consequences for Man City or exonerated them.

"If Man City find themselves at the wrong end of a verdict, it'll be the end of the decade before it's concluded.

"So, if it goes against Man City, it will be the end of the decade because they will bring an appeal.

"If it goes against the Premier League, the Premier League won't bring an appeal against it, even though, they were the ones who brought the action.

"It is what it is, and people are screaming from the rooftops about what Man City are doing, but Man City need to keep running their business.

"Everyone is questioning how they can spend £450million, but they didn't because they sold nearly £300million worth of players."

2 Jordan would like to see City publicly demanding an outcome because they insist they are innocent Credit: talkSPORT

State of play

Eight-time Premier League winners City are accused of breaching financial rules from 2009 to 2018.

The majority of the charges relate to not providing accurate financial information, not complying with UEFA's FFP and not revealing managerial compensation.

And 35 other charges are related to City not cooperating with the Premier League's investigation.

And Jordan believes that with City's stance insisting they are totally innocent, they should be demanding a resolution to the case.

"The Premier League clubs are paying for it," he added.

"If I am Man City, but I am waiting for two years to exonerate myself, I would be up in arms.

Man City's charges explained 1. Failure to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information from 2009-10 to 2017-18. 54 charges relating to breach 2. Failure to provide accurate financial reports for player and manager compensation from 2009-10 to 2017-18. 14 charges relating to breach 3. Failure to comply with UEFA's regulations, including UEFA's Club and Licensing and Financial Fair Play Regulations. Five charges relating to breach 4. Breaches of Premier League profitability and sustainability regulations from 2015-16 to and including 2017-18 season. Seven charges relating to breach 5. Failure to cooperate with Premier League investigations from December 2018-present 35 charges relating to breach

"I would be saying, 'where is this verdict? 'Because it is an absolute outrage that our name is being besmirched.'

"But it is strange that they are silent about it. I would have thought there would be more outrage.

"Surely, they must be infuriated. Why wouldn't they be shouting from the rooftops about where is the verdict."

Premier League's view

Man City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023, but there is still no outcome regarding the charges.

And speaking to talkSPORT in August, the Premier League's CEO Richard Masters was asked about the situation by our Chief Football Correspondent Alex Crook.

He said: "I obviously can't comment on it. I do understand the frustration. It has taken longer than expected, but we have to follow the process."

Crook then asked if it was damaging the Premier League, and Masters responded: "I hope not.

"In the end, the Premier League's responsibility is to ask the Independent Commission to look at serious allegations and to establish the truth.

"That shouldn't be qualified by it taking too long, for example."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi can extend record trophy haul and end MLS drought in newly-created fixture
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has the chance to win his 48th career trophy on Wednesday night as Inter Miami eye a historic victory.

Messi currently holds the record for the most trophies ever won by a player, and he's now on the brink of extending it.



4 Messi has won 47 trophies across his career and now has the chance to extend his record with a 48th in the Campeones Cup Credit: AFP

The footballing legend will line up for Inter Miami in the Campeones Cup, which was only officially launched in 2018.

Mexican champions Cruz Azul will be their opponents, as the MLS winners and LIGA MX winners clash in the fixture.

The one-off match was created alongside the Leagues Cup - which is a tournament that includes clubs from the USA, Canada and Mexico - to help 'strengthen the sport in the region'.



Inter Miami have never played in the game before, meaning this is a chance for them to lift the trophy for the first time.

Their success in the MLS last season put them forward for the Campeones Cup and they will feel they need to beat Cruz Azul, not just for themselves or Messi, but for the league as a whole.



The American sides have lost to their Mexican opponents in every edition of the fixture since 2022.

LA Galaxy lost to Toluca last year, with Columbus Crew losing to Club America in 2024 and LAFC being beaten by Tigres in 2023.



Lionel Messi's record trophy haul

Messi is hoping to get his hands on his fourth trophy as an Inter Miami player at the $1billion Nu Stadium.

He has won 47 pieces of silverware across his iconic career, including four Champions Leagues and 10 La Liga titles.

The 39-year-old picked up those trophies with Barcelona, where he won 34 in total, while he also won Ligue 1 twice during his short stint with French giants Paris Saint-Germain.

4 Messi lifted the MLS Cup for Inter Miami last season, which qualified them for the Campeones Cup final against Cruz Azul Credit: Getty



Lionel Messi: Notable trophies won LaLiga : 10x (2004–05, 2005–06, 2008–09, 2009–10, 2010–11, 2012–13, 2014–15, 2015–16, 2017–18, 2018–19)

Champions League: 4x (2005–06, 2008–09, 2010–11, 2014–15)

Ligue 1: 2x (2021–22, 2022–23)

MLS Cup: 2025

Copa America: 2021, 2024

World Cup: 2022

On the international stage, Messi completed football by winning the World Cup with Argentina in 2022.

Either side of that incredible success, he led his country to Copa America glory, taking his tally to three international titles.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner, who has been nominated for the award again this year, is three clear of any other player when it comes to trophies won throughout his career.

His tally of 47 is three more than former Barcelona teammate Dani Alves, who won 44 and four more than PSG's Marquinhos, who has won 43 in his career so far.



And he sits a huge 12 titles clear of rival Cristiano Ronaldo, with the Portuguese icon lifting 35 trophies in total.

Messi can extend that gap with an Inter Miami victory against Cruz Azul, with the Campeones Cup clash taking place at 8pm local time on Wednesday night, which is 1am on Thursday in the UK.

4 Messi's World Cup win is sure to be the standout in his record-breaking collection of trophies, which beats Ronaldo's by 12 titles Credit: Getty

Campeones Cup past results 2018: Toronto FC 1-3 Tigres

2019: Atlanta United 3-2 Club America

2021: Columbus Crew 2-0 Cruz Azul

2022: New York City 2-0 Atlas

2023: LAFC 0-0 (2-4 on penalties) Tigres

2024: Columbus Crew 1-1 (4-5 on penalties) Club America

2025: LA Galaxy 2-3 Toluca

Who has won the Campeones Cup before?

As mentioned, MLS clubs haven't had the best luck in the Campeones Cup in recent years, with the Mexican sides dominating.



Toluca are the most recent winners, as they beat LA Galaxy 3-2 last year, with Club America succeeding in 2024.

They beat Columbus Crew on penalties - the same method that Tigres won the trophy over LAFC the year prior.

The last MLS team to win the Campeones Cup was New York City in 2022 amid early dominance from the Americans.

In the first four editions of the match, it was Atlanta United, Columbus Crew and New York City that came out on top.



So, can Inter Miami and new manager Kily Gonzalez join that exclusive group and bring the trophy back to the States?

4 Messi has a strong record against Mexican sides and he will hope to add another win on Wednesday Credit: Getty

What is Messi's record against Mexican teams?

Well, Messi's record against Mexican clubs certainly gives Inter Miami a good chance of getting their hands on the silverware.

He has played 10 times against Liga MX teams throughout his career in the USA and with Barcelona, losing just once.



The now-retired Argentina international has won five and drawn four in such outings across competitive games and friendlies.

For Miami, Messi has scored three goals in five clashes against teams from Mexico, including one against Cruz Azul.

Altogether, he's netted six times in his 10 such games.

Sports.title: Arsenal approached for perfect Max Dowman loan move by EFL club
Sports.content:
Luton Town have previously requested to take Max Dowman on loan from Arsenal, the club's senior scout has revealed.

The Hatters are managed by former Gunners midfielder Jack Wilshere.

4 Wilshere has tried to sign Dowman on loan for Luton multiple times, says Mick Harford Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Following Dowman's latest eye-catching display, it has been revealed Luton have tried to to sign the 16-year-old on multiple occasions.

The winger scored twice in a 4-2 win over Ipswich Town in the third round of the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night.

It has taken his tally to three goals in 14 first-team appearances for Arsenal since his debut in August 2025.

And Hatters head scout and club ambassador Mick Harford has lifted the lid on their interest in the teenager.

Luton eyed Dowman

He has revealed Wilshere spoke to Gunners boss Mikel Arteta about the possibility of taking Dowman on loan at Kenilworth Road.

When asked about Dowman on talkSPORT, Harford replied: "I think Jack's asked him a couple of times, Mikel, but I don't think he'll be going out on loan."

Dowman previously played under Wilshere for Arsenal's Under-18s during his time as manager.

He scored two goals and provided seven assists in 12 appearances under his fellow Hale End graduate.

The 34-year-old has been in charge of Luton since October having been handed his first senior managerial role.

Wilshere has since won 25 of his 51 matches in charge as well as lifting the EFL Trophy last season.

4 Dowman scored twice in Arsenal's win over Ipswich on Tuesday night Credit: Getty

Dowman and Wilshere compared

Harford has also compared Dowman's emergence to Wilshere's rise through the Arsenal academy.

The Hatters legend added: "Jack was a wonderful footballer, he still is on the training ground.

"He started, not as a wide man, but as a wide man tucking in those little pockets, getting on the ball and creating stuff.

"Dowman looks more of a wide man than a pocket player, but a wonderful talent.

"I think he will get more game time and I think if he produces, I think Arteta will play him.

"I'm a believer in if you're ready, I don't care what age you are. If you're good enough, you'll play and I'm sure he will. He looks like he's going to be a superstar."

4 Comparisons have been drawn between Dowman and a young Wilshere due to their wonderkid status Credit: PA:Press Association

Wilshere made his Arsenal debut aged 16 under Arsene Wenger back in 2008.

He went on to make 197 appearances for his boyhood club, scoring 14 goals and adding 28 assists from midfield.

The former England international also won two FA Cups with the Gunners as well as featuring 34 times for the Three Lions.

Following an injury-ravaged career, Wilshere retired from professional football aged 30 in 2022.

As well as his time at Arsenal, he also had permanent spells with West Ham, Bournemouth and Danish side Aarhus.

After retiring, Wilshere began his coaching career with the Gunners' Under-18s before spending the 2024/25 season at Norwich.

4 Wilshere has been in charge of Luton since October last year Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

During his time at Carrow Road he served as Johannes Hoff Thorup's assistant before a two-match spell as caretaker boss.

Having left the Canaries in May last year, Wilshere is less than a month away from celebrating 12 months as Luton boss.

The Hatters currently sit 12th in League One after six matches this season.

Under Wilshere, they ended last term in seventh, missing out on the play-offs by a single point.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi handed two month sack warning after ‘slightly embarrassing’ Liverpool defeat
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi has been warned the pressure could crank up on him if Tottenham Hotspur lose this weekend.

However, former Premier League midfielder Danny Murphy believes De Zerbi will not be sacked before November despite Spurs' winless start to the season.

3 De Zerbi has been warned he could come under pressure if Spurs lose to Aston Villa this weekend Credit: AFP

The north London outfit have taken just two points from their opening four Premier League matches without scoring a goal.

Meanwhile, Spurs were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Liverpool on Tuesday night.

Murphy has labelled their 3-1 defeat at Anfield a 'little bit embarrassing' but still expects Spurs to finish in the top half this term.

De Zerbi's side host Aston Villa on Saturday, live on talkSPORT, in their final match before the international break.

Murphy backs De Zerbi

Another loss would not be enough for the Italian to be sacked, though, according to Murphy.

Instead, he expects the Spurs hierarchy to give him up to another two months once the club returns to action in October.

Speaking on White & Jordan, Murphy admitted: "They’ll climb up the table. I still think they’ll be in the top half.

"I am surprised how poorly they’ve started, but actually the turnover of players, a lot of new players have come in, some of them late. He’s not yet established his best 11.

"There’s a few decisions when you watch them play. I’ve done most of the games where it’s kind of a little bit baffling, but they’ve got enough.

"It’s just about getting through this initial bad spell. Last night didn’t help.

3 Murphy has labelled Spurs' defeat to Liverpool a 'little bit embarrasing' Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"I think he picked a strong team, which he should have done because he’s under a bit of pressure.

"He’s got a lot of quality and competition for places, but he picked a really strong team and they played okay.

"They missed a couple of big chances in the first half which can change momentum in a game, but to lose 3-1 it’s a little embarrassing.

"There comes a point with every manager at every club where the fans will start and if they lose to Villa at the weekend before the international break, all of a sudden amazingly he’s under pressure.

"Even if they lose at the weekend, I still think they’ll give him a month or two after they get back from the international break."

What's next for Spurs?

Spurs face a three-week gap between matches after Saturday's 12:30pm kick-off against Villa due to the season's first international break.

3 De Zerbi's side are yet to score or win in the Premier League this season Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Following the match, their next fixture will be away to Manchester United on October 10.

Heading into the weekend, Spurs sit 17th in the Premier League after back-to-back goalless draws against Nottingham Forest and Everton.

Those results follow defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United to start the season.

De Zerbi was appointed Spurs manager in March on a five-year deal through to the summer of 2031.

Having guided the club to three wins from seven matches to end the season, he secured their top-flight survival on the final day of the campaign.

A home win over Everton saw Spurs finish two points clear of London rivals West Ham, who were relegated to the Championship.
