Sports.title: These are desperate days for Man United: After derby defeat and academy star JJ Gabriel's public snub, it gets even worse for Michael Carrick as Brighton fight back to knock them out of the Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
What desperate days these are for Manchester United.

Beaten in the Old Trafford derby on Sunday, at odds with their own fans and snubbed by the superstar of their academy, it felt as though things couldn't get any worse. Until this.

Two goals up against Brighton on Wednesday night, United were beaten at home for the second time in three days as they crashed out of the Carabao Cup at the first attempt for the second year in a row. At least Brighton aren't Grimsby.

It had all looked so promising when 19-year-old Shea Lacey celebrated his first start with a goal. It felt like it was meant to be following the shock news that his Under-21s team-mate JJ Gabriel - who could also have played in this game - announced he wanted to quit the club.

Mason Mount put United two up, but Brighton roared back to win for the fifth time in six visits to Old Trafford with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim de Cuyper.

It was also the first in 146 games that United have lost at home after being two goals ahead.

Maxim De Cuyper wheels away in celebration after scoring Brighton's winner vs Man United

Michael Carrick saw his United side lose a 2-0 lead to get knocked out of the Carabao Cup

It's been a tumultuous few days for the Red Devils on and off the field and this only adds to it

After all the furore over Gabriel, the stage was set for Lacey to carry the torch for United's academy and he didn't disappoint.

Ironically, his first start came against Brighton who were United's opponents for Lacey's home debut at Old Trafford in January - in the last game before Michael Carrick took over from caretaker Darren Fletcher - which ended in despair for the youngster when he came on as a substitute and was swiftly sent off for two bookable offences.

Lacey has stayed at the front of the queue of academy players pushing for a first-team place since then, and Carrick rewarded him as he made six changes from the Manchester derby.

'We've always had hopes for Shea,' said the United boss before kick-off. 'Balanced hopes, you know, because you never want to get too carried away.

'We're not putting everything on him. It's not one chance, one game and that's it. But it's certainly a good opportunity for him.'

If Carrick was concerned about putting too much pressure on the boy, he need not have worried.

There was something inevitable about the fact that he fired United ahead. Noussair Mazraoui played the ball to Youri Tielemans, United's £35m summer signing who was captaining the team on his sixth appearance, and the Belgian picked out Lacey on the right side of the box.

He was marked closely by Jaouen Hadjam, but Lacey took one touch to control the ball and two more to get it out of his feet and wide of the Brighton defender before whipping a shot inside Jason Steele's near post.

Shea Lacey kisses the Manchester United badge after opening the scoring in the match

United doubled their lead on 10 minutes when Mason Mount scored with this right-footed shot

Old Trafford rose to salute the first teenager to score on his United debut since Marcus Rashford against Midtjylland here a decade ago. Lacey kissed the badge and Carrick raised both arms to the fans behind the dugout in the Sir Bobby Charlton Stand.

They had only just settled down when Mount had them off their seats again in the 10th minute. Rashford picked Costinha's pocket on the other flank and breezed past Luka Vuskovic. Steele kept out his effort but the ball ran to Mount who got there just ahead of Lacey to score the second.

At that stage, it looked like being an easy night for United. Rashford looked particularly dangerous down the left where he had Costinha on the run and delighted the fans when he nutmegged Chema Andres.

But Brighton were not about to lie down after conceding two goals in two minutes and began to put pressure on a defence that had youngsters Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven at the heart of it.

Heaven was caught out in the 27th minute by Matt O'Riley whose cross was cut out by Yoro, and Olivier Boscagli fired narrowly over the bar of United's debutant goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

Malick Yalcouye should have scored when he was sent clear by Gross, hotly pursued by Heaven, but placed his effort wide of Darlow's far post, and it needed a brilliant sliding tackle by Tielemans to deny Kostoulas.

When Kostoulas got Brighton back into the game in added time at the end of the first half, it was the least they deserved.

United were unhappy that referee Farai Hallam didn't give Benjamin Sesko a free-kick when he was floored by a tag team of Yalcouye and Boscagli, but they switched off and Hadjam's long diagonal pass picked out Kostoulas who had got away from Heaven. The Greek controlled the ball before knocking it past a hesitant Darlow.

Charalampos Kostoulas started the Brighton comeback with this shot just before half-time

Pascal Gross (second right) levelled the scoreline for the Seagulls with this left-footed finish

It felt as though Carrick needed to make changes at half-time to alter the flow of the game but none were forthcoming.

Instead, Brighton continued to push after the restart and equalised in the 64th minute. Diogo Dalot kicked a clearance towards halfway where Sesko was under pressure from behind by Pascal Struijk and succeeded only in heading the ball 30 yards back towards his own goal where Gross was waiting to receive it on the edge of the box. He sold Yoro a dummy before sliding a shot past Darlow.

Bryan Mbeumo, Joshua Zirkzee and Kobbie Mainoo were waiting to come on at the time, but their introduction couldn't prevent Brighton shocking Old Trafford by going ahead.

Kostoulas got away from Mazraoui in the 69th minute and closed in on Darlow's goal. His cross got a deflection off the Moroccan and fell for substitute De Cuyper who slotted in the third to pile more misery on Carrick and his players.

Sports.content:

Liverpool will entertain Chelsea in a blockbuster all-Premier League encounter in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

The clash, the pick of the ties in Wednesday's draw, will see former Reds midfielder Xabi Alonso return to Anfield for the first time since taking over at Stamford Bridge.

Elsewhere, Arsenal will travel to League Two side Fleetwood Town, who are in the fourth round for the first time in their history after beating Sheffield United 1-0.

Fleetwood are the lowest-ranked side left in the competition and play at the aptly-named Highbury Stadium.

The Gunners, last season's beaten finalists, thumped Ipswich 4-2 on Tuesday night.

Holders Manchester City play their third round tie against Norwich City on Thursday, and the victor of that match is set to entertain Brighton.

Liverpool will entertain Chelsea in the pick of the Carabao Cup fourth-round ties

Everton, searching for their first major trophy since 1995, will play Newcastle, who won the Carabao Cup in 2024-25, at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Bournemouth have been handed a home tie against Aston Villa after Unai Emery's side picked picking up their first domestic victory of the season at Coventry on Wednesday via a 3-1 triumph.

Bradford City and Peterborough are the only two League One representatives still in the competition and they have been drawn against each other, with the Bantams set to host that game.

The fourth round matches will all be played in the week commencing October 26, rather than being split over two weeks like the third round was.

Sports.title: Aston Villa heap misery on Frank Lampard's Coventry with 3-1 Carabao Cup victory... it's early days but this season is already looking alarming for the Sky Blues, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Aston Villa heap misery on Frank Lampard's Coventry with 3-1 Carabao Cup victory... it's early days but this season is already looking alarming for the Sky Blues, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Frank Lampard is learning that even when you lead a club to promotion, management can feel a horribly lonely place when it starts to go wrong.

The former England midfielder guided Coventry back to the top flight for the first time in 25 years but just six games into their campaign, it is already looking alarming. Their defending was awful here, particularly from set pieces, and there were some boos in the second half.

‘When you concede simple goals like we did from set pieces, it’s hard to win against Premier League opposition,’ Lampard said. ‘It’s mentally difficult for players. The soft nature of the second and third goals meant it wasn’t easy to come back.’

The Carabao Cup will not determine Coventry’s season. However, they have now lost five of six in all competitions as Aston Villa claimed their first victory in domestic football this term. Two goals from Tammy Abraham – who was given his chance by Lampard at Chelsea – and another from Ross Barkley sent Villa into round five, with Victor Torp’s first-half equaliser a rare bright moment for Lampard’s team.

Villa boss Unai Emery will be encouraged by Ibrahim Mbaye’s exciting performance, which could earn him a starting spot at Tottenham on Saturday. Villa made seven changes to Coventry’s nine, and both conceded far too many chances. However, there was still no place for Alejandro Garnacho, who has played just 31 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea.

Tammy Abraham scored twice as Aston Villa beat Coventry City 3-1 in the EFL Cup third round

Unai Emery wanted Abraham to leave this summer, but the striker silenced the doubters here

It was another brutal result for Frank Lampard and his side must dramatically and quickly

‘It’s about working and training,’ said Emery. ‘When he has minutes to play, he must try and play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now.’

Emery was not thrilled that Abraham decided to stay at Villa rather than join Ipswich on loan and in the early exchanges, the Villa boss berated his forward twice for failing to follow instructions.

Abraham answered in the best way possible. George Hemmings collected a pass from full debutant Matteo Ruggeri and slipped Abraham through for a calm finish beyond Dan Bentley.

Villa looked in control until Barkley trod on the ball and fouled Caleb Yirenkyi just outside the Villa box. From the free-kick, Torp curled in Coventry’s first home goal of the season.

Last time these clubs met, in 2001, Coventry lost 3-2 at Villa Park and were relegated from the top flight. They have been all the way to League Two and back since then and the equaliser made them believe once more.

Bobby Thomas robbed Tyrone Mings inside the box but instead of shooting, tried to tee up Sidiki Cherif for a debut goal. Then Gustavo Hamer’s dipping effort flew just wide.

Neither side’s defence was remotely convincing and Ibrahim Mbaye was enjoying his first start for Villa. The £50m signing’s shot rebounded into the path of John McGinn who shot wide, before Barkley went close from 25 yards.

Bentley tipped that one wide but from Mbaye’s corner, Barkley was left alone on the edge of the six-yard box to head Emery’s men back in front.

There was still time before the break for Cherif to shoot straight at Marco Bizot when he should have picked out a team-mate. That would be reserve keeper Bizot’s last involvement as he was replaced by Zion Suzuki for the second half.

If Coventry’s marking was bad for the second goal, they surpassed themselves for the third. This time McGinn drilled a low bar that was dummied by Barkley and Hemmings and steered home by Abraham inside the six-yard box. Not one of the Sky Blues players inside the box had attempted a clearance.

Sports.title: Enzo Le Fee's magic lit up the Stadium of Light to inspire Sunderland to an unforgettable 1-0 win over AZ Alkmaar - and the Black Cats showed why they belong in Europe, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
He arrived in the Championship but is deserving of the Champions League. For now at least, Enzo Le Fee is the reason Sunderland are playing, and winning, in the Europa League.

Just when this big occasion demanded a big player to conjure a big moment, the little magician from Brittany reached into his bag of tricks, bamboozled AZ Alkmaar’s defenders and cast a spell over a home crowd that will last a lifetime. They will not forget this night.

It was in the 65th minute that Le Fee won and then converted the penalty that meant Sunderland’s first European fixture in 53 years ended in a deserved victory. No player deserved that place in the history books more than him. He had illuminated the Stadium of Light long before his goal, just like he did last season. The 26-year-old, once of Roma, is a special, special player. He, just like the occasion, did not disappoint.

‘You need good players in the right moment,’ said Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris. ‘And Enzo is a great player. He can create, he can score, he can help in defence. Yes, he’s great!’

Sunderland’s stadium took its name from one of European football’s greatest venues, Benfica’s Estadio da Luz. Opened in 1997 with the dream of continental nights like this, as recently as five years ago there was not so much light as the darkness of League One. It was Accrington, not Alkmaar. Morecambe, not Milan.

Enzo Le Fee coolly converted his second-half spot-kick to earn Sunderland a mighty 1-0 win

His penalty earned Sunderland victory over AZ Alkmaar in their first European game since 1974

MATCH FACTS Sunderland (4-2-3-1): Roefs 8; Mukiele 7, Danso 7, Alderete 6 (Ballard 52, 7), Reinildo 6; Xhaka 7, Sadiki 6; Hume 7, Le Fee 9, Fofana 5 (Angulo 67, 6); Isidor 6 (Brobbey 67, 6) Subs: Moore, Ballard, Methalie, Rigg, Meunier, O'Nien, Ahoka, Jones, Tutierov, Proctor Manager: Regis Le Bris 6 Referee: J Pignard (FRA) 7 Man of the Match : Le Fee

But this is not the story of a plucky underdog, dining at a table at which they do not really belong. Sunderland should be playing in Europe. Sunderland should wave their flags and plant them loudly and proudly on foreign soil this autumn. Come spring, Sunderland should still be in this competition. They’re here not by winning a cup - as they last were in 1973 - but by finishing seventh in the world’s strongest league.

This game was not really about the result, either. It was about ‘I was there’, and I want to be here again. Half a century and more is a long time between European nights. The last one came at Roker Park, against Sporting Lisbon, in a competition that no longer exists. There are supporters here who have lived through an entire generation between continental visitors. For others, this was the first taste, sight and smell of something they had only ever watched and imagined happening elsewhere. For the majority, this was not European football coming back to Wearside, it was the arrival of it.

That was certainly the pervading feeling among those on the playing side. Le Bris and captain Granit Xhaka have been singing from the same hymn sheet this week, chorusing the message that this is just the start, not the final destination. It was, however, never going to be an understated opening to this chapter.

The guttural release when the teams emerged, the same raw sound when League One survivor Trai Hume took out Ayoub Oufkir and the giddy shrieks of the barely believable when Le Fee almost scored direct from an early corner all ensured that the action on the pitch satisfied the anticipation in the stands. This was good. Great, even. Sunderland were playing in Europe, and they were playing well.

Defender Kevin Danso, scorer of one League Cup goal in three years at Tottenham, went in search of the Puskas Award with a 25-yard dipper tipped over by Jari De Busser. Le Fee’s shot then tested the base of the post and this stadium’s plastic seating, given the 48,000 who crashed back into theirs in despair. Or maybe that’s the wrong word, because there was nothing despairing about Sunderland’s performance.

But Alkmaar were good, too. That helped. This felt proper. Loaded with academy products, we will no doubt see the likes of midfielder Kees Smit and forward Ro-Zangelo Daal in the Premier League at some point, even if at inflated fees. Maybe Sunderland, of Europe, will be shopping in that market.

To get here, their recruitment has been rather more shrewd. Take Xhaka. Rarely will £17m be better spent on a player north of 30 years old. To the left of him, on the wing, was a team-mate who could represent the future direction, £31m deadline-day signing Malick Fofana. Not that the Belgium international, 21, appears on the same page as his colleagues just yet.

The page-turner, rather, was Le Fee.

The spirited Black Cats proved why they belong back in Europe on an unforgettable night

There was, though, a period around the hour that was something of a European tutorial for the home side. Their energy, understandably, had faded. AZ took charge, teasing and weaving passes and patterns. How would Sunderland respond? Well, give the ball to Le Fee, of course.

And so, in the 64th minute, he weaved a pattern of his own, right through the penalty area. Just as he was about to shoot, he was tripped. Penalty. He missed last weekend against Arsenal. He was not missing this one.

Sports.title: Man United 2-3 Brighton PLAYER RATINGS: Which player endured a 'very difficult night'? Who did himself no favours after falling down the pecking order - and which three stars disappointed with 4/10 displays?
Sports.content:
Man United 2-3 Brighton PLAYER RATINGS: Which player endured a 'very difficult night'? Who did himself no favours after falling down the pecking order - and which three stars disappointed with 4/10 displays?

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United crashed out of the Carabao Cup as boos rang out at Old Trafford on another damaging night for Michael Carrick.

Brighton were 2-0 down and reeling 10 minutes in after goals from Shea Lacey, marking his first start, and Mason Mount.

United had never lost from the previous 145 games when 2-0 up at Old Trafford but there was a nervousness in the air, not least when Charalampos Kostoulas made it 2-1 just before half-time.

Carrick's side never got a grip on this topsy-turvy game thereafter and goals from Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper condemned United to a Carabao Cup exit at the first attempt for the second successive season.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT gives his verdict on Carrick's charges as they bow out of the Carabao Cup…

Brighton produced yet another emphatic performance here at Old Trafford in the Carabao Cup

Michael Carrick looked furious on the touchline at the end as Manchester United crashed out

MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1)

Karl Darlow – 5

Senne Lammens provides a calmness that others can build off but Darlow seemed to do the opposite on his United debut. Was far too indecisive in coming for Jaouen Hadjam’s through ball that Charalampos Kostoulas scored from. Too often seemed to get his positioning wrong but made a crucial stop late on to keep United in the game for a bit longer.

Diogo Dalot – 4

Never quite got to grips with Brighton’s threat down his side and was given a warning when he switched off and didn’t track the run when Malick Yalcouye ran through the lines to be clear on goal, only to shoot wide. His reckless and aimless hooked clearance left United all at sea for Brighton to score their second goal. An experienced player who didn’t use his experience with so much youth surrounding him.

Leny Yoro – 5

Only his second start of season and this wasn’t a ringing endorsement for more. The young Frenchman did make a number of key interceptions in the first half but neither he nor Heaven looks like the vocal leader in the Harry Maguire mould that any good partnership needs. Looked all at sea for Brighton’s third goal. Deserves some credit for the crucial block he made to stop a near-certain goal with 10 minutes to go.

Ayden Heaven – 4

A very difficult night. Was caught in two minds when both he and Darlow hesitated on the stroke of half-time for Brighton to get their first, found himself way too far from Yoro to leave a gaping hole for the second and was not alert to the danger for the third as he missed the key challenge when Noussair Mazraoui had already blown his assignment.

Ayden Heaven endured a difficult night as Brighton came from 2-0 down to win it 3-2

Noussair Mazraoui – 5

Took a nasty whack from Costinha 20 minutes in and required lengthy treatment but carried on. Plays left back for Morocco and was doing OK here before his deficiencies showed and Brighton exposed his lack of pace for the decisive third goal.

Youri Tielemans – 7

Wearing the captain’s armband, Tielemans came out of this as United’s best player, albeit not a high bar to clear. His vision picked out Lacey for the opening goal and he worked hard at the other end when he made a brilliant last-ditch challenge on Kostoulas late in the first half to deny a goal. Showed some pieces of skill that were highlight worthy, but again like Dalot, Carrick needed to see an experienced player do more to stop the bleeding in a game like this.

Andrey Santos – 5

Had played less than 45 minutes since starting away at Hull City having fallen down the pecking order. This was a rare opportunity and while the Brazilian did make some key interceptions, this wasn’t a performance that exactly made a compelling case for regular starts.

Shea Lacey – 6

A magic moment for a special young player. Lacey was making his first career start for United and netted, in typical Lacey fashion for those who watched him in the academy, his first senior goal, a stunner. Produced a brilliant spin move on the touchline to bamboozle Hadjam, who got a booking for dragging him down. Faded slightly but a bright spot on another grim night.

Shea Lacey became the first United teenager in a decade to score on their first start

Mason Mount – 5

Scored the second goal of the game in smart fashion by crashing an effort into the ground and then the roof of the net. But on a night where he had every chance to take control of a game in the No 10 position that is forever locked down by Bruno Fernandes, Mount became a non-factor after the goal. The disappointment on his face when he came off said it all.

Marcus Rashford – 6

Gave Costinha nightmares and his pace is such a valuable weapon to United. But he had the chance to equalise when through one on one. He looked offside but no flag came and it was a wonder save by Steele to deny him. A player of Rashford’s quality has to score that, though. Was a defining moment on the night.

Benjamin Sesko – 4

Did produce some clever touches to bring team-mates into play and was inches away from nicking the ball past an onrushing Steele as Brighton’s back-pass attempt fell short before the hour. But he didn’t manage a single effort on goal in 65 minutes before coming off on a rough night. It doesn’t feel like he or United know how to get the best out of him.

MANAGER: Michael Carrick – 4

Turn that pressure dial up a notch. He demanded more intensity from his players as this one got away from them and by the end he had his stars out there trying to salvage a cup run. It was all in vain and the noise around his position only gets louder from here.

SUBS

Bryan Mbeumo (for Shea Lacey, 65) - 6

Joshua Zirkzee (for Benjamin Sesko) - 5

Bruno Fernandes (for Mason Mount, 73) - 6

Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes were unable to rescue the tie as United crashed out

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho is already playing catch-up at Aston Villa - if his chance does not come at Coventry tonight, the ex-Man United man may wonder when it will, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho is already playing catch-up at Aston Villa - if his chance does not come at Coventry tonight, the ex-Man United man may wonder when it will, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Since joining Aston Villa, Alejandro Garnacho has played only 31 competitive minutes and received a flea in his ear from his manager. As first impressions go, it has been far from ideal.

Garnacho is not the only Villa player to be told off in public by Unai Emery this season for dawdling on the touchline before being introduced as a substitute.

Yet even though we are still in mid-September, it feels like the 22-year-old is already playing catch-up. He was not helped by a facial injury sustained in pre-season which meant Villa did not pick him for the UEFA Super Cup in mind-August.

With Emery expected to rotate his squad for Wednesday's Carabao Cup tie at Coventry, Garnacho will expect to be involved.

Garnacho’s loan will become a £43million transfer next summer if he hits what Chelsea claim are ‘easily achievable’ targets at Villa. All sorted, then? Not quite.

Alejandro Garnacho will be desperate to start his first game against Coventry on Wednesday

Difficulties settling in

Not many attackers join Villa and start playing regularly straightaway. Morgan Rogers managed it and so has Nicolas Jackson, but Emery has worked with Jackson before and when the Villa boss saw Rogers in the Middlesbrough team in January 2024, it was love at first sight.

Rogers joined Villa for about £10m and never looked back. Now he has gone to Chelsea for £117m. Few absorb Emery’s instructions as quickly as he did.

‘It’s a demanding style and very unique system,’ said captain John McGinn. ‘A lot of work in the classroom.

‘It does take time. It’s not just a case of your normal 4-4-2 or your normal 4-2-3-1. It’s the detail but it’s different. It’s like me going to play international football – it’s a different kind of football. You just need to adapt and hopefully over time we start to grow.’

Emery’s decision to stick to who he knows has not worked this season. Of the new signings, only Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and midfielder Joao Gomes have earned his trust, with Ibrahim Mbaye, Matteo Ruggeri and Taylor Harwood-Bellis also looking to make their mark along with Garnacho. Johan Manzambi has only just returned from injury and Leon Goretzka is sidelined with a knee problem.

Garnacho has managed just 31 competitive minutes since joining Villa in the summer

The ghost of Harvey Elliott

Villa might not like to hear it, but loans can be complicated. Last September the club brought in Harvey Elliott from Liverpool on an initial loan deal, which would have become a £35m transfer had the midfielder played at least 10 times.

Elliott made nine appearances across the season, with Emery deciding last November that he did not want him. That left Elliott in limbo for the rest of the campaign with Villa paying a significant salary contribution for a player they knew would rarely feature.

While Garnacho is not at that stage yet, the Coventry match feels big for him. As things stand, it is difficult to imagine the Argentine starting at Tottenham in the Premier League on Saturday.

If he is given a chance at Coventry and takes it, however, at least Garnacho will give Emery something to think about. ‘His attitude his positive,’ said Emery. ‘That is very important.

‘Now he needs time, and hard work every day, which is showing in his attitude. He has played a few minutes and it was not enough – first, the minutes he played and second, the things he showed.

‘But progressively I am seeing him better. The most important thing is to be consistent and demanding in his attitude, and then I believe he will gradually really his best performance.’

Garnacho's situation feels fairly similar to that of Harvey Elliott's at the club last year

Competition for places

The problem for Garnacho is that the battle for spots out wide is fierce. George Hemmings has emerged from Villa’s youth ranks and immediately made an impression on Emery, starting every game so far.

Mbaye may be only 18 but he has not moved for £50m to swap the Paris Saint-Germain bench for the Villa one, while McGinn is not going anywhere either.

Alysson has looked impressive when given the chance this term, and scored Villa’s first league goal of the season. When Manzambi is fully fit, he will probably play as a No10, with Buendia moving back to the wing. So when does Garnacho get his chance?

‘We want to see him at the same level he was at in the first part of the season last year at Chelsea, and before that at Manchester United,’ Emery stressed. ‘He has this challenge, and it’s my challenge to help him achieve it.

‘He needed time to adapt to us and to get his fitness, and there is still work to do. But we have signed him for a long time and we will help him feel comfortable with us, feel confident with us and to exploit his qualities in our tactical structure.’

Garnacho’s best years were 2023-25, when he scored 20 goals and had 17 assists for Manchester United. Find that form again, and the permanent move to Villa becomes a formality. First, Garnacho needs consistent playing time. If that opportunity does not come at Coventry on Wednesday, those around Garnacho may start to wonder when it will.

Sports.title: Liverpool Confidential: Latest on new deal for Rio Ngumoha revealed, the clubs keen to poach him, why he's guaranteed more minutes this season, how Lewis Koumas reached 'dreamland' and injury updates on three key defenders
Sports.content:
Liverpool have issued a hands-off warning to clubs circling Rio Ngumoha and remain extremely keen to extend his contract.

There has been a flurry of talk about the 18-year-old’s future in the last week with Arsenal mooted as a club following his situation. Bayern Munich also expressed an interest in the summer transfer window.

Sources have told Confidential that the Gunners’ interest is not advanced and more exploratory. It is genuine, however, with the English champions keeping tabs on the situation in case the teenager struggles for game-time and gets itchy feet following the arrival of two new wingers – Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz – at Anfield.

Liverpool, though, would not entertain any offers for Ngumoha. His contract runs until 2028 and they plan to keep him beyond that. They see him as a future world-beater and believe he will get plenty of minutes this season.

It is understood Ngumoha is aware of interest from elsewhere – not just Arsenal and Bayern Munich – but is happy at Liverpool.

Ngumoha signed a three-year professional contract on September 25 of last year. That was the longest deal a player of his age could sign and the club also has a salary cap for youngsters – though the player will be remunerated well from bonuses.

Liverpool are keen for Rio Ngumoha, 18, to extend his contract at the club

Ngumoha could be named in the England squad for their upcoming Nations League matches. He shone on debut in a World Cup warm-up match in the United States

Sources close to the situation this week insisted there is no update on a new contract just yet but Ngumoha is enjoying life at Anfield. Liverpool are keen to reward him for his meteoric rise in the last 12 months.

Ngumoha moved to Liverpool in 2024, when they poached a winger described as the best talent in Chelsea’s academy. A tribunal ruled in February that the Reds must pay £2.8million to Chelsea, which could rise to £6.8m with bonuses.

He made his senior England debut in a World Cup warm-up match, starring against New Zealand. Thomas Tuchel is a big fan and Ngumoha could be named in the England squad announced this Friday for upcoming Nations League matches.

Ngumoha started against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League and Tottenham in the Carabao Cup in the last week and although he might privately feel uneasy about the arrival of £123m Barcola, the teenager will get lots of minutes this season given Andoni Iraola’s desire to rotate his wide men.

He started nine times last season and is already nearly halfway to matching that tally this time after just one month of the campaign. Due to his tender age, Liverpool were careful with his minutes last term.

They will still not push too much, too soon but Ngumoha is now trusted for more starts and longer appearances than mere cameos. Iraola likes to change his wingers mid-game which means all four – Ngumoha, Barcola, Cody Gakpo and Munoz – will get lots of game-time.

Ngumoha faces competition for his place from Liverpool's new £123m signing Bradley Barcola

Clubs including Arsenal and Bayern Munich have shown an interest in Ngumoha

KOUMAS IS IRAOLA'S DREAM

Confidential readers will recall last week’s musings on how it was obvious why Iraola adores Lewis Koumas. If it was not evident then, it is plain to see now.

The Chester-born forward is living his dream and it is especially pertinent when there was a lot of talk this summer about the lack of a local academy graduate in the first team in light of Curtis Jones’s exit to Inter Milan.

Geography experts will (rightly) contest the suggestion Koumas is a Scouser but the 20-year-old has grown up around the academy, having joined aged 11 from Tranmere Rovers, who were annoyed about their talented kid being poached.

Koumas has had a crack at breaking through before. He was an unused substitute a few times under Jurgen Klopp in the German's final season, including in the Carabao Cup final, and started an FA Cup tie against Southampton in February 2024.

He scored in front of the Kop but might have thought his Liverpool career would be limited to just one appearance after he was loaned out to Championship sides Stoke, Birmingham and Hull.

Those loans were positive but it would also be fair to say he showed few signs that he was ready to crack it on the biggest stage. When Koumas was left on the bench for the Tigers’ play-off final success, he could not have seen the next few months unfolding as they have.

‘I would have woken up!’ he said, laughing, when asked how he would have reacted then if someone had told him he would soon make his Champions League and Premier League debuts, then win man of the match in the Carabao Cup against Tottenham.

‘I would have thought I was dreaming. It’s crazy. But I’m just really happy and very grateful for the opportunities I’ve been given.

Lewis Koumas impressed with his high-energy style against Tottenham yesterday

Koumas credits his time on loan - including a spell with Hull City last season - as vital to his development

‘I never showed a weak mentality about how the future would look for me at Liverpool. I always had the drive that I would get here. The reason for going out on loan was to prepare for this moment.

‘The past two years have been massive for my development. Going on loan helped me become the player I am today. I was able to impress the new manager in pre-season and it all worked out well.’

Confidential reported in our first column of this season that Koumas, midfielder James McConnell and defender Luke Chambers were set to stick around despite huge interest in taking them on loan. It is understood Iraola made that decision early in pre-season due to their versatility, attitude and tactical skills.

Koumas, son of former Premier League midfielder Jason, can play as a striker, winger, No 10 and even operated as a wing-back for Hull. He is liked for his relentless and clever pressing, which is perfect for Iraola’s style of play.

It is reductive to simply say he is a good runner, as he is also adept on the ball. He scored important goals for Hull last season and does not seem fazed by big occasions.

The Wales international, who turns 21 next week, grew up idolising Gareth Bale and Michael Owen – though the latter's Liverpool career was slightly before his time. ‘How I play is ultimately the Liverpool way,’ Koumas added on Tuesday night.

‘We’ve always been a club where players have to give absolutely everything on the pitch. We’re bringing that back now and the crowd are loving it. You never know when your last time on the pitch for Liverpool is going to be. I just try to leave everything out there every time.’

The best word to describe Koumas is one from Iraola: ‘Contagious.' His running sets the tone for others and his story – with those loans in the lower leagues – should inspire other youngsters that development might not always be linear.

Right now, young buck Koumas must feel on top of the world – but he will hope this is only the beginning.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (right) describes Koumas as 'contagious'

ZIDANE AND KLOPP TO GET HANDS ON LIVERPOOL STARS

International squads are to be announced in the coming days with some interesting news lines to watch from a Liverpool perspective.

Does new France boss Zinedine Zidane reward the impressive Jeremy Jacquet with a first senior cap? Does new Netherlands manager Xavi stick by captain Virgil van Dijk, who will turn 37 during the next Euros? Will Ngumoha get that England call-up?

Former Barcelona midfielder Xavi also has a decision to make over Jeremie Frimpong, who was omitted from the World Cup squad and has struggled in the early weeks of this campaign.

Klopp will get his first chance to work with Florian Wirtz at Germany, too. The midfielder has shown glimpses of class this term but is yet to discover any consistency.

Former Reds boss Klopp could help him along the way. The Liverpool legend has been working his way around Bundesliga stadiums but is yet to be spotted at Anfield to run the rule over Wirtz.

Meanwhile, young Liverpool full back Isaac Mabaya has switched allegiances to Zimbabwe and accepted a first call-up after previously featuring for England’s age-group sides. He made his first-team debut at Plymouth in February 2025 but has been plagued by injuries since.

The 21-year-old went on loan to Wigan but was recalled to do rehab work at the AXA Training Centre.

Will the new France boss Zinedine Zidane reward Liverpool's impressive defender Jeremy Jacquet with a first senior cap?

And will Virgil van Dijk, who will turn 37 during the next Euros, still be key to the Dutch national team?

ROLE-MODEL MILNER COACHING KIDS

James Milner has returned to Liverpool to gain experience in his coaching journey – and give his own experience back to youngsters.

The 40-year-old recently called time on a stellar player career that spanned 24 years and saw him break the record for most Premier League appearances. He is now working towards his UEFA Pro Licence and is helping out with coaching some of the younger age groups on a casual and not permanent agreement.

It is a similar story with Conor Coady, who has been spotted at the AXA Training Centre several times in recent months. He is on Lee Carsley’s England Under-21 coaching team.

James Milner is coaching with Liverpool as he works towards his UEFA Pro Licence

INJURY LATEST: BRADLEY AND LEONI STEP IT UP

There is light at the end of an extremely long tunnel for two Liverpool defenders.

As documented in this column in previous weeks, Giovanni Leoni is stepping up his recovery from an ACL injury that has seen him miss nearly exactly a year.

Right back Conor Bradley is also on the comeback trail and is now training alone, doing ball work after a knee injury suffered in January. Small steps on both counts but positive to hear.

Federico Chiesa has been missing for several weeks but is aiming for a late-September return to training. He and Wataru Endo have been omitted from the European squad list.

And Joe Gomez went off at half-time on Tuesday night and fans feared the worst given it was the injury-prone defender’s first game of the season after a lay-off. But it was a planned substitution – he is OK and in contention to make the squad for Bournemouth on Sunday.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick points the blame for 'unacceptable' Man Utd surrender vs Brighton
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick points the blame for 'unacceptable' Man Utd surrender vs Brighton

Manchester United crashed out of the Carabao Cup after throwing away a two-goal lead at home to Brighton to pile pressure on manager Michael Carrick

View 3 Images Michael Carrick speaks after Man Utd's 3-2 defeat to Brighton at Old Trafford (Image: Sky Sports)

Michael Carrick blasted Manchester United’s surrender as “unacceptable” after they crashed out of the Carabao Cup.

‌



United blew a two-goal lead and the Old Trafford faithful then turned on the players with loud boos at the final whistle.

‌



It leaves Carrick under mounting pressure as it was the first time in 50 years that United have lost a game after going 2-0 up at home in any competition.

‌



United boss Carrick said: “We can't accept that as a group. I take responsibility for it. The performance towards the end of the second half, that's on me.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"We'll all be better. We have to be better. We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We're out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

"It doesn't feel good at the moment. It doesn't feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That's all I'm thinking about right now.”

Carrick admitted he could understand the feelings of the supporters as they booed loudly at the final whistle. It was loud and angry and left the United boss under genuine pressure.

‌



View 3 Images Man Utd crashed out of the Carabao Cup at Old Trafford

Carrick added: “"Yeah of course, that's pretty obvious! I totally understand the feelings of the supporters.

“We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It's on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I'll take the praise, I'll take the criticism and the upset.

‌



“I totally understand it for the way the game went. We have got to win games."

View 3 Images Carrick has asked for patience regarding the JJ Gabriel situation (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Carrick also pleaded for patience and understanding after United wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, told the club he wanted to quit.

Article continues below

Carrick added: “We have to be a little bit careful on that one. He's a 15-year-old boy. It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child really.

“He's certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we have to be careful about the exposure and how much we jump on that."

Sports.content:
Carabao Cup fourth round draw as Arsenal and Liverpool discover opponents

Carabao Cup holders Manchester City could face Brighto in the fourth round after the draw was made with last year's losing finalists Arsenal taking on Fleetwood

View Image Last season's Carabao Cup finalists, Man City and Arsenal, remain in contention (Image: Alfie Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Manchester City will face Brighton in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup provided they beat Norwich on Thursday night whilst Premier League leaders Arsenal will take on Fleetwood Town.

‌



Liverpool will face Chelsea in one of the ties of the round having downed Tottenham on Tuesday night. 2025 winners Newcastle have landed a tie against Everton. Manchester United will again be absent for this round after their embarrassing loss to Brighton.

The Gunners made light work of Ipswich on Tuesday night and will seek to win the Carabao Cup for the first time since 1993. Mikel Arteta has fallen short in the semi-final and the final in successive years but will aim to take the final step this season.

Sports.title: Man Utd fans turn on Michael Carrick's side as Brighton defeat piles pressure on boss
Sports.content:
THE mood inside Old Trafford turned as quickly as the score line.

At the final whistle, there was a chorus of boos as the Manchester United faithful turned on the players. And if Michael Carrick was not under pressure before, the United boss is certainly feeling the heat now.

This was unforgivable. A lame, meek surrender as United threw away a two-goal lead with some kamikaze defending and unforgivable play.

Incredibly, this was the first time United had blown a two-goal lead in 146 matches and they find themselves out of another domestic cup competition. Again.

‌



Last season, United went out at the first hurdle in the Carabao Cup and FA Cup (the latter to Brighton) and endured the shortest season in the club’s history.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It did, however, allow Carrick to turn the club’s fortunes around, guide them back into the Champions League and got the job as a result.

‌



But, after a sloppy start to the Premier League campaign - including the Manchester derby to City on Sunday - and now an early cup exit maybe this is proof they plumped too soon with a club legend.

Passion and history will get you so far but Carrick now looks to be struggling as they were hit by their Brighton curse again. That is five wins out of six trips to Old Trafford for the Seagulls.

And it was a pure gift for Fabian Hurzeler’s never-say-die heroes. What a win. But what a lame surrender and an awful week for United.

After teenage wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, told the club he wanted to leave, the script turned around when academy graduate Shea Leacey scored on his first start for the club. What a time to get your first goal with a lovely finish after just eight minutes.

‌



It got even better two minutes later when Mason Mount made it 2-0 and surely not even a sloppy United could blow it from here. Don’t bet on it.

View 3 Images Manchester United have been dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton

They did not put the game to bed and were sloppy in defence, the star-studded bench left them short on the pitch and Brighton refused to give up.

You could see Brighton grow in confidence while United began to drop deeper and leave themselves increasingly vulnerable.

‌



They got their reward in first half injury time. Jaouen Hadjam’s diagonal ball split the United defence, Brighton striker Charalampos Kostoulas then fired low past keeper Karl Darlow and it was game-on.

United just did not do enough to put Brighton away. And Brighton just kept going. Diogo Dalot’s clearance was headed straight back by Luka Vuskovic and the ball fell for Pascal Gross.

Brighton forward Gross sidestepped Lenny Yoro, kept his nerve and then fired low past Darlow to level it up. United made it easy. Yoro was exposed that time but Ayden Heaven was so far out of his depth.

View 3 Images Maxim De Cuyper completed the fantastic Brighton comeback at Old Trafford

‌



Brighton were still not done. Kostoulas broke down the right edge of the box, his pull back fell straight to Maxim De Cuyper and suddenly Brighton were in front.

You could hear the boos and frustration begin to ring round Old Trafford as Brighton had turned the game on its head and United were facing another cup nightmare.

Marcus Rashford went through but was denied by Steele. United threw on the big guns to try and salvage a terrible week. But they did not have enough guile, quality or determination to turn it around. Another early cup exit. Another nightmare for Carrick.

Suddenly United’s trip to Fulham on Sunday looks very big for Carrick. Especially as it comes just before the international break.

‌

Sports.title: Man Utd crash out of the Carabao Cup after crumbling vs Brighton - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Manchester United's season went from bad to worse as they gave up a 2-0 lead to lose to Brighton and go crashing out of the Carabao Cup.

Goals inside the opening ten minutes from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount looked to have set the home side on their way to a much needed win, given the difficult start to their campaign.

But Pascal Gross, who scored his eighth goal against the Red Devils, helped the Seagulls record yet another win over the side from Manchester. United hadn't given up a two-goal lead to lose at Old Trafford since the 1970s, but that stat went up in smoke.

Charalampos Kostoulas pulled a goal back in first-half stoppage time before Gross equalised midway through the second-half. Maxim De Cuyper completed the comeback on the 70 minute mark to send shivers around Old Trafford.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lacey's strike after eight minutes came after he cut in from the right, taking his left-footed shot early, which flew into the near post. The Old Trafford crowd still reeling from that strike were celebrating again within two minutes.

Mount, who himself has found opportunities hard to come by, was able to seize on an error of Brighton's own making as they attempted to play out from the back. The United midfielder struck his volley into the ground, with the bounce seeing it nestle into the Brighton net.

‌



The Seagulls rallied and eventually got their reward in first-half stoppage time. Kostoulas was able to finish from an acute angle to half the deficit. Little did he know it would ignite a historic comeback. Gross' equaliser owed to some poor defending as a headed clearance from the halfway line found the Brighton man unmarked on the edge of the United box before he turned and finished.

View 4 Images Pascal Gross continued his impressive scoring record against Man Utd

De Cuyper's winner came from close range as he converted after a neat comeback before running towards the corner where the travelling supporters were enjoying another day out in Manchester.

Marcus Rashford missed United's best chance to level as he was denied from close range as the Red Devils saw their Carabao Cup hopes ended at the first hurdle once again. Here's five talking points from Old Trafford.

‌



Brighton jinx continues

In recent years few teams have enjoyed greater dominance over United than the Seagulls, who have made beating them an annual event. Brighton headed to Old Trafford having won seven of their last eleven games against the Premier League giants.

That includes a 2-1 win in Manchester in the third round of the FA Cup last season. That run of form also saw Brighton beat United in the first game of the Erik ten Hag era, that another win at Old Trafford, and a 4-0 mauling back in 2022 when the Red Devils were at one of their lowest ebbs.

You may have thought that a two-goal head start would've been enough to see United get the better of Brighton, but no, the Seagulls recorded another impressive win - their eighth in their last 12 against the Red Devils.

Game mismanagement

Throughout the season United have faced criticism for failing to manage games and, worryingly for them, conceding goals. Sunday was one of the rare occasions they didn't concede twice during a game, but that trend returned on Wednesday as Brighton breached the United goal on numerous occasions.

‌



View 4 Images Michael Carrick had no answers as his side lost for the third time this season

Perhaps a greater frustration for Carrick will the apparent inability of his side to manage games, especially when leading. They failed to see out the contest at Everton recently, conceding late. Against the ten-men of Manchester City they also failed to make it count. But the loss to Brighton by far and away topped the lot.

Lacey's moment

The last time Lacey faced Brighton at Old Trafford he was thrown on after an hour, but failed to see the full-time whistle after being shown a red card. The teenager cut a despondent figure when he walked down the tunnel, thinking one of his early opportunities to impress had come and gone.

Eight months after that forgettable moment the teenager, handed his first start of the season, needed just eight minutes to score the first goal of the night. There are high hopes for Lacey, even in an attack that has established quality, and the 19-year-old's first goal of his career could not have come against a better opponent, even if his efforts will be forget on what was a difficult night for those in red.

‌



View 4 Images Shea Lacey's strike was the perfect start for the hosts

No place for JJ

All the talk regarding United over the past 24 hours is shock as they deal with the bombshell news that JJ Gabriel, one of the most highly thought of players to come through the academy for some time, wants out.

The sensation was named Under-18 Premier League player of the year last season, even though he was only 14 when the campaign began, underlining his potential. He was poised to make his debut against Brighton, but instead is looking for a way out of Old Trafford. His name alongside the No 77 was printed on the back of the matchday programme, but his stay in Manchester could be over before its started.

Sesko pressure remains

In the opening weeks of the season there's been constant theories as to why Carrick doesn't seem to fancy Sesko, at least as a starter. The Slovenian grew into his debut season, coming off the bench to score multiple winners, but a bench player he has remained.

‌



Instead players who aren't natural No 9s have been deployed in those positions ahead of Sesko. But when the former RB Leipzig man got the nod on Wednesday night he did little to push his case for more involvement, especially from the start. Being hooked on the hour mark was not a ringing endorsement.

Sports.title: Liverpool send clear message to Arsenal over 'genuine' plan to poach Rio Ngumoha
Sports.content:
Liverpool send clear message to Arsenal over 'genuine' plan to poach Rio Ngumoha

Rio Ngumoha has transfer interest from Arsenal but Liverpool have a clear stance on selling the young attacker

View 2 Images Liverpool star Rio Ngumoha is not for sale amid transfer interest from Arsenal (Image: (Photo by James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Liverpool have reportedly issued a hands-off warning to Arsenal and other clubs interested in signing Rio Ngumoha. Bayern Munich were linked with a move during the summer transfer window, and now the Gunners have emerged as a club that wants to sign the exciting winger.

‌



Ngumoha joined Liverpool from Chelsea in 2024 and signed a three-year professional contract 12 months ago. He has made 35 appearances for Liverpool's senior team, with Andoni Iraola continuing to give him more minutes this season.

‌



The 18-year-old started Tuesday's Carabao Cup third round win over Tottenham, but Arsenal are keeping a close eye on whether his minutes decrease following the arrivals of Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz, according to The Daily Mail.

‌



Liverpool news: Reds confirm midfielder return as star admits regret at Anfield exit READ MORE :

Arsenal handed final verdict as Premier League panel unanimously agree on red card decision READ MORE :

However, it has been claimed that Liverpool have no plans to entertain any offers and remain keen on agreeing a new contract with the teenager. Interest from Arsenal is understood to be genuine, but a deal is not advanced.

He has two years left on his current deal and Liverpool want to keep him beyond that as there is a belief he can become a 'world-beater'.

Ngumoha is believed to know of the interest from elsewhere, but he is enjoying life and is therefore happy at Liverpool. There is also no current update on contract talks between the two parties.

‌



Arsenal's hope that Ngumoha will become restless appears far-fetched as the winger has already been deployed from the off in four games this season, which means he is nearly halfway to the nine starts he managed last season.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

One of those was the Champions League clash against Atletico Madrid, with Ngumoha speaking fondly of the experience and the trust placed in him by Iraola.

‌



“It was crazy,” Ngumoha told the club’s website. “In the morning when I knew when the gaffer put out the team, I saw my name there. I was like, 'Yeah, today's going to be a good day!'

“A first start in the Champions League, especially at Anfield and against a good side. To get the three points and just hear the fans, like I said the other day, Anfield was roaring, I couldn't ask for much more.

View 2 Images Ngumoha was buzzing to start Liverpool's first Champions League game of the season

‌



“Like I said, the gaffer, [for him] to put faith in me and to show me that he believes in my abilities and qualities to help the team get a win is really positive. I couldn't ask for much more.”

Ngumoha started on his favoured left side in that game, but has been needed on the other flank a few times already, with all of Barcola, Munoz and Cody Gakpo preferring to play on that side.

The latter can play as the striker, while Munoz has performed admirably when on the right with his tireless work ethic, earning praise. He also scored his first Liverpool goal when on that side, with a superb strike against Nottingham Forest.

Article continues below

The four have shared minutes so far with Ngumoha set for a considerable amount of game time, given the competitions Liverpool are in this season.

Sports.title: Andy Burnham watches Everton with Canadian leader Mark Carney  who also lost his dad to Alzheimer's
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham watches Everton with Canadian leader Mark Carney who also lost his dad to Alzheimer's

Despite grieving his dad, Andy Burnham continues to work — and today he had an engagement with Prime Minister of Canada, Mark Carney, who joined him to watch Everton play Wolves

Andy Burnham joins Canadian PM Mark Carney for Everton game

Prime Minister Andy Burnham's meeting with Mark Carney held emotional significance tonight — as the Canadian leader shared he too lost his dad to Alzheimer's disease.

‌



The politicians were pictured united in the stands at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium where they watched the club they both support play Wolverhampton Wanderers in a Carabao Cup tie. The Toffees won the game 1-0 and now David Moyes' side are in the hat for the draw for the next round, which will be held tonight.

‌



Both leaders wore Alzheimer's Society forget-me-not flowers on their lapels, and Mr Carney revealed he had also lost his father to the disease, telling Mr Burnham: "I know that struggle." A photo of Roy Burnham, who died earlier this week, was shown on the stadium's big screens before kick-off and a tribute was made at half-time.

‌



Words alongside the picture, displayed to the 50,970 fans present, read: "RIP Roy Burnham. Lifelong, direhard Blue, much loved by Eileen, Nick, Andy, John and all the family."

Andy Burnham vows 'unwavering' Nato support amid Russia warning READ MORE :

View 3 Images Andy Burnham and Mark Carney went to watch their beloved Everton (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

Posing for photographs in front of British and Canadian flags in the directors' clubroom, Mr Burnham had said: "What a real, life privilege this is for me to welcome the Prime Minister of Canada.

‌



"We share so much, Mark - we have a few Liverpool connections, Ireland connections, but, of course, Everton connections - and it's going to be a special occasion."

Mr Carney said the first Everton match he ever attended was the 1989 FA Cup semi-final - the game that took place on the day of the Hillsborough disaster, which Mr Burnham has also spoken about attending. Mr Carney praised Mr Burnham for his role in "bringing justice and closure" for the families of the 97 Liverpool fans who died.

View 3 Images A tribute to Andy Burnham's dad, Roy, was played on the big screen at the venue (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

‌



Mr Burnham described the former Bank of England governor as a "great progressive leader" and pointed to potential future co-operation on defence and AI.

"It's just so good for me to think I will have somebody to talk to and commiserate about Everton at a G7 meeting," he said. "You are so welcome to Liverpool and, obviously, to your beloved club - the new home of Everton."

Mr Carney said there was scope for the two countries to "build together", including on shared values around AI. "It is an honour to be here. It is a pleasure to be here," he added.

‌



After the 45-minute meeting, the pair swapped suits for blue and white Everton scarves and took their seats in the stands, shaking hands and posing for photos with supporters along the way.

Mr Burnham first invited Mr Carney to a match when the two spoke in July, shortly after he took office. Mr Carney adopted Everton as his team after moving to the UK, while Mr Burnham has been a regular at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, which opened last year, since becoming Prime Minister.

View 3 Images Everton's Jack Grealish has a shot on goal during the match at the Hill Dickinson Stadium (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

‌



Speaking today, Michelle Dyson CB, Chief Executive of Alzheimer's Society, said: "Alzheimer's Society's Forget Me Not badge is proudly worn by people across the UK, and it is incredibly powerful to see both the UK and Canadian Prime Ministers wearing it on the international stage.

“We're grateful to both leaders for speaking so openly about their personal experiences of dementia. By sharing their family's stories, they are helping to shine a light on the realities of the condition and sending an important message that dementia can touch any family, anywhere in the world.

“Our Forget Me Not badge is worn as a symbol of remembrance, understanding and solidarity with everyone affected by dementia. It helps raise awareness of the condition, challenges stigma and sends a powerful message to people living with dementia and those who care for them that they are not alone.

Article continues below

“Alzheimer's Society is here for anyone affected by dementia. Visit alzheimers.org.uk or call our Dementia Support Line on 0333 150 3456."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel can't watch Argentina collapse back - but now accepts blame for agonising exit
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel can't watch Argentina collapse back - but now accepts blame for agonising exit

England manager Thomas Tuchel initially blamed 'England's footballing DNA' for their heartbreaking World Cup defeat to Argentina - but now admits he made a big mistake

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel admitted he went defensive too early during England's heartbreaking defeat to Argentina

Thomas Tuchel has revealed he has still not been able to watch back England’s World Cup semi final defeat as it was an “agony of epic proportions.”

‌



England boss Tuchel admitted he went defensive too early against Argentina because he felt his side were waiting for “death” with the game slipping away from them.

‌



Tuchel was talking on the FA’s Reflections show and said he could only bring himself to watch clips of the game with his other coaches at St George’s Park last week.

‌



But Tuchel admitted that he has not watched the game in its entirety and, while reviewing the Argentina heartbreak, repeated back some commentary which he says summed it up.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Tuchel said: “Agony of epic proportions. I watched the clips with my coaches just last week when we were at SGP.

“My mind always works forward, forward. Painful. I see it now for the first time from the commentators’ point of view. It’s my scar, the players’ scar, I have to live with it. No-one is hurt more than me. It is torture.”

Tuchel said after the Argentina defeat that part of the problem was down to England’s DNA and a failure to keep the ball rather than negative tactics.

‌



But on reflection, Tuchel said that he got it wrong when he saw the game slipping away from England even before Anthony Gordon gave them the lead. Argentina’s late comeback knocked England out.

View 3 Images England suffered more World Cup agony after failing to hold on against their old rivals (Image: Getty)

Tuchel admitted they were outwitted and outsmarted by Argentina and their experience together with their tactics.

‌



Tuchel added: “We relied on our brotherhood, our mentality. Individual quality. Argentina have that as well - brotherhood, mentality, they bring it all to the table and it means the world to them.

“You have to have football quality. We prepared so well. I think we did quite well in the first half, it was quite an even match and I felt we were there.

“But from the start of the second half, I saw a change. The famous tackle of Djed Spence. And it did something to me, it did something to the players and it was a shift in the mindset. We played like we had four minutes left but there was half an hour left.

‌



View 3 Images Tuchel claims the brilliant tackle by Djed Spence changed his and the England players' mindsets

“Argentina played very, very quickly. They had nothing to lose. We conceded a chance just before the water break. I thought we will not survive. This is death.

“I thought: ‘OK, let’s change to a back five, a 5-4-1.’ It was too early for that mindset. It was Congo, Miami and Norway and then Mexico and altitude. We were super tired.”

Article continues below

Tuchel says, however, beating France to finish third does count. “You learn as a coach. You have to play as if it is 0-0. That includes me as well,” he said.

“I have a lot of people who want to see my medal. We did not achieve what we wanted. But I am still very proud of what we achieved. These players will come back hungry.”

Sports.title: Biggest VAR blunders ranked after Man City's derby winner leads to Enzo Maresca swipe
Sports.content:
The VAR fallout rumbles on, as it always does. The Manchester derby is the latest game to be embroiled in controversy that stems from decisions taken at Stockley Park.

Erling Haaland's strike was enough to land Manchester City the three points on Sunday, leaving those associated with Manchester United fuming. Michael Carrick didn't shy away from lamenting the decision in the aftermath of the game.

Pro Ref chief Howard Webb has quickly come out and owned up to the error live on TV, after the organisation itself had issued an apology to United within hours of the final whistle.

Once again the issue of VAR and those using it is front and centre. Since 2019 we've had the system in use, and yet the sceptics seem no closer to being converted. Even some of those in favour initially have veered towards binning it, letting mangers and players live with decisions as we did for decades.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

City boss Enzo Maresca has claimed the reaction to the VAR blunder, which failed to acknowledge that Enzo Fernandez had thrown himself at the ball from an offside position, had been overblown.

"Talking about one episode or one moment after that game when we played for 70- 75 minutes with 10 players, I think it's quite poor," said the Italian.

‌



He too claimed that some decisions go for you, some go against you. Maresca even went as far as to reference another VAR mishap in a Manchester derby in 2023, when he was an assistant to Pep Guardiola. The refereeing body didn't apologise for that one.

View 6 Images VAR awarded the goal after it was initially ruled out for offside (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Any mistake that lives with someone for three years is clearly noteworthy, but we haven't lacked for errors of that magnitude. So what really is VAR's darkest day? We've had a go at ranking the biggest injustices, but make sure you have a go at putting them in order yourself using our interactive tool.

5. Haaland's derby winner

The latest one that's got us all talking. Haaland's strike on Sunday was initally ruled offside, and it looked it, but once the lines had been drawn it was deemed that Patrick Dorgu had played him onside.

‌



That part is accepted, what isn't accepted is that Fernandez had no bearing on the play. The Argentine midfielder was stood in the middle of the box in an offside position and threw himself to try and head the ball, but missed. Lisandro Martinez was clearly impeded as he attempted to cover Fernandez and Haaland.

VAR claimed that because Fernandez didn't touch the ball, all was cleared. Failing to acknowledge the fact he clearly impacted the play. Gary Neville said that he expected an apology pretty soon, and one duly arrived.

4. Rodri dodges handball

During the 2021/22 title race City went to Goodison Park and scored late on via Phil Foden as they looked to pick up a priceless three points. That was soon in doubt though, when Rodri looked to have handled the ball in his own box.

The Spaniard misjudged the bounce of the ball and, as he went to control it on his chest, looked to have seen the ball strike his arm instead. The home crowd were adamant and, such was the length of the VAR check, it was clearly a tight call.

‌



View 6 Images Rodri escaped any punishment as VAR overlooked this handball shout (Image: Sky Sports)

To the naked eye it looked as if the City talisman had made a rare error, but somehow he and Pep Guardiola escaped. Lampard accused the VAR official Chris Kavanagh of being a “professional who cannot do his job right”. Then referees’ chief Mike Riley would personally apologised to Lampard, for whatever that was worth.

3. Fernandes goal given

The one Maresca just refuses to forget. In 2023 City took the lead at Old Trafford before two goals from United turned the game. Bruno Fernandes' strike levelled the game and came despite Marcus Rashford being offside by several yards.

The United attacker raced after the ball and had in it his path, albeit he didn't touch it, but his presence undoubtedly influenced the City defenders. Fernandes then raced from an onside position to score. The offside flag went up, but the officials then reversed their decision as the hosts went on to land a winner.

‌



View 6 Images Marcus Rashford was clearly offside and chased after the ball, but didn't touch it, with Man Utd profiting as a result (Image: Sky Sports)

"Rashford is offside. Bruno Fernandes is not offside. The question is intervening or not intervening in the action," said Guardiola. "When one player shoots and [another] player is in front of the keeper and does not touch the ball, it's disallowed all the time."

Webb later claimed: “I think if that exact circumstance happens again you would probably see a different outcome".

2. Onana punch overlooked

In Erik ten Hag's second year at the helm he decided to rid of David de Gea and bring in Andre Onana, a move that would not prove overly successful. On his first outing the warning signs were evident with the Cameroonian.

‌



As United looked to close out three points in their opening fixture against Wolves, who had been more than good value for a point if not more, Onana had a moment of madness and came out to punch clear a cross, but instead caught Sasa Kalajdzic. No contact made with the ball, but contact certainly made with the Wolves player in the dying stages.

View 6 Images Andre Onana collided with Wolves star Sasa Kalajdzic, but dodged any punishment

No penalty though. Then Wolves boss Gary O'Neil said elite referees manager Jon Moss told him he "could not believe" the error. The three officials involved were overlooked the following weekend.

1. Diaz goal ruled out

Liverpool's first defeat of 2023 came at Tottenham on an evening when Luis Diaz thought he'd scored the opening goal of the night, only to quickly see the offside flag raised.

‌



It looked a tight call to the naked eye and so VAR jumped in to confirm the linesman's call. The glaring issue? They thought the call was onside, so when they 'agreed' with the on-field call, they were agreeing it was offside.

The PGMOL called it a "significant human error" and the audio, later released, showed immediate panic and several people not on the same page. Explicits rang out once they realised the gravity of the error and, after the game restarted they couldn't call it back and simply had to live with their mistake.

View 6 Images Luis Diaz's wrongly disallowed goal at Tottenham three years ago remains one of VAR's darkest days (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Then Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp was quizzed on the apology from the PGMOL but replied: "We won't get points for it. We all thought that when VAR came in it would make things easier."

‌

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
